policy: Released base-game lore and story; full text is opt-in behind spoiler controls. Unreleased DLC is excluded.

factions.name: Aegis Alliance
factions.description: A defensive pact of independent colonies who value protection and community above all.

pages.text: The Aegis Alliance was formed by a collection of independent outer colonies who grew tired of being pawns in the endless war between Horizon and Aurora. United by a common desire for mutual protection, the Alliance is a bastion of defensive technology and stubborn resilience. They are not conquerors; they are guardians.

Their Warmachines, like the Bulwark and Sentinel, are built to endure. Favoring heavy armor, powerful shields, and coordinated defensive tactics, the Aegis Alliance excels at holding the line against overwhelming odds. Their pilots are not glory-seekers, but protectors, fighting for their homes and their families.

'The Last Bastion' is the embodiment of the Alliance's core principle. It is not designed to win wars, but to end them. Its shield systems are tied into the very bedrock of the colony it defends, drawing power from the collective will of those it protects. It is a fortress with a heart, and it has never fallen.

factions.name: Cygnus Corporation
factions.description: A shadowy mega-corporation that plays all sides, dealing in espionage and black-ops technology.

pages.text: While Horizon represents the public face of corporate power, Cygnus Corporation is the shadow it casts. Officially a neutral entity specializing in logistics and R&D, Cygnus is in fact a ruthless intelligence network that profits from the endless war. They sell their technology—and their secrets—to the highest bidder, manipulating conflicts from the shadows to maximize their bottom line.

Their technology is sleek, subtle, and deadly. Specializing in stealth, electronic warfare, and bio-augmentation, Cygnus frames like the Spectre and Blackout are designed for assassination and corporate espionage. Their pilots, known only as 'Agents' and 'Assets', are products of intense conditioning, their loyalty bought and paid for.

Asset designation: 'Null Sector'. A frame so secret, its existence is denied even on the highest corporate servers. Its purpose is not combat, but erasure. Utilizing stolen Zenith phase technology, it does not destroy its targets; it removes them from the timeline. A hostile takeover of reality itself.

factions.name: Kingdom of Aurora
factions.description: A traditional, honor-bound monarchy that values duty, chivalry, and heritage.

pages.text: The Kingdom of Aurora is a feudal society built on ancient traditions of honor, loyalty, and martial prowess. Ruled by a monarch and a council of noble houses, the Kingdom sees itself as a bastion of civilization and culture against the cold, sterile pragmatism of Horizon and the savagery of the outer clans. Their code of chivalry is both their greatest strength and their most exploitable weakness.

Auroran Warmachines, such as the Paladin and the Gekkou, are often works of art as much as they are instruments of war. Ornate, durable, and favoring close-quarters combat with energy blades and heavy shields, they reflect the Kingdom's focus on the individual skill and valor of the pilot, their 'knight'.

The Kingdom's rigid adherence to tradition has led them down dark paths. Desperate to counter Horizon's technological edge, certain elements within their command structure initiated the 'Oni Program'—a monstrous project designed to create a pilot with absolute loyalty and no hesitation, a perversion of their own code of honor. The tragic fate of Ensign Kaito is a testament to this hidden corruption.

Lieutenant Hikari's defection was a blow to the heart of the Kingdom's identity. As heir to a noble house, her betrayal was seen as an unforgivable stain on her family's honor. Her alliance with a Horizon pilot was an act of treason that challenged the very foundations of Auroran society.

The 'King's Guard' is not a single machine, but a title bestowed upon the frame that protects the monarch. Forged from alloys found only in the heart of the capital's oldest mountain, its armor is said to be unbreakable. It is the final shield, the last line of defense, the embodiment of the Kingdom's vow to endure.

factions.name: Liberté
factions.description: A loose confederation of independent pilots, mercenaries, and idealists.

pages.text: Born from the ashes of forgotten colonies and corporate betrayals, Liberté is not a nation but an idea: that every pilot has the right to choose their own destiny. They are a chaotic but passionate faction, their ranks filled with everything from grizzled mercenaries to young idealists fleeing the rigid doctrines of the two great powers. Their strength lies in their unpredictability and the fierce loyalty they hold for one another.

Liberté's technology is a hodgepodge of stolen, salvaged, and heavily customized parts. A Liberté Warmachine is a reflection of its pilot—unique, often unreliable, but capable of surprising feats of brilliance. They are masters of improvisation, turning scrap into weapons and hopeless situations into victories. This resourcefulness makes them a constant thorn in the side of both the Republic and the Kingdom.

While they lack a formal command structure, charismatic leaders like the enigmatic Marianne have been known to rally disparate cells under a single banner for a common cause. They fight for freedom, for the forgotten, and for the simple right to exist in a galaxy that demands conformity. Their ultimate goal is not conquest, but a future where no one has to kneel to a king or a corporation.

The pilot known as 'Joto Rinto' and their experimental frame, the 'Apex Pilot' project, are seen by many in Liberté as a symbol of their struggle. An individual with extraordinary power, hunted by the very system that created them, who chose to fight for a cause greater than themselves. Their story is a legend whispered in the back-alley cantinas and hidden asteroid bases of the free pilots.

The Apex Project was a Republic failure, but in the hands of a free pilot, it became a legend. The 'Revolution' is not merely a machine; it is the physical manifestation of Liberté's will. It is a one-frame rebellion, a ghost that haunts empires, a promise that as long as one pilot is free, the war is never truly over.

factions.name: No Faction
factions.description: Mercenaries, independents, and mysterious entities who walk their own path.

pages.text: In a galaxy defined by monolithic powers, there are always those who refuse to choose a side. This category encompasses a vast array of individuals and machines: lone mercenaries, wandering Ronin, experimental frames of unknown origin, and pilots whose pasts are shrouded in mystery. They are wild cards, their allegiances often shifting with the tides of war and the weight of their coin purses.

Their technology is as diverse as they are, ranging from aging but reliable frames to bizarre, one-of-a-kind prototypes. They are a testament to the fact that even in a galaxy at war, the individual spirit—for good or for ill—can never be fully extinguished.

The 'Ouroboros' is a paradox, a machine that should not exist. Rumored to have been built by a pilot who fell through a singularity, it exists in a constant state of self-repair and self-destruction. It is the beginning and the end of the cycle of war, a wandering enigma that answers to no one.

factions.name: Red Wolves
factions.description: A brutal faction of outcasts and warlords who believe the old world must burn.

pages.text: The Red Wolves are a nomadic, fiercely independent faction born from the lawless frontier zones. Led by the charismatic but ruthless ideologue Matsuo, they are a loose coalition of clans who believe the great powers are corrupt beyond redemption. Their philosophy is simple: burn it all down and build a new world from the ashes, a world forged in fire and ruled by the strong.

Their machines, like the savage Cerberus Frame and the monstrous Bahamut, are patchwork horrors of stolen and salvaged technology. They are brutally effective, prioritizing raw power and psychological terror over finesse. The Red Wolves are masters of ambush and guerrilla warfare, a constant, unpredictable threat to the supply lines and outposts of both major powers.

Beneath their chaotic exterior lies a cunning intelligence. Strategists like Kingu, a disgraced Horizon officer, have given the Red Wolves a tactical edge that belies their savage appearance. They are not merely raiders; they are a revolutionary force with a clear and terrifying vision for the future.

The Red Wolves' role as agents of chaos was solidified during the disastrous Citadel peace conference. Exploited by corporate interests and driven by their own destructive ideology, they shattered the fragile truce between the great powers. Pilots like the unhinged Tiamat became symbols of their terror, but it was Matsuo's cold, calculating vision that guided their hand. They are not simply raiders; they are a catalyst, a wildfire burning away the old world to make way for their own brutal order.

Ragnarok. The end of all things. It is not a machine built for conquest, but for annihilation. Powered by a volatile, scavenged core from a doomsday device, it exists only to see the galaxy burn. It is the Red Wolves' final, nihilistic promise: if they cannot have a new world, no one will have one at all.

factions.name: Republic of Horizon
factions.description: A technologically advanced, corporate-military state that values efficiency and progress above all.

pages.text: The Republic of Horizon rose from the ashes of the old world's corporate sector. Governed by a council of directors and a powerful military, Horizon society is built on the principles of logic, efficiency, and relentless technological advancement. They see themselves as the galaxy's guiding hand, bringing order and progress to the lesser factions, whether they want it or not.

Horizon's military is a marvel of precision engineering. Their Warmachines, like the Shrike and Ballista, are sleek, advanced, and built for specific tactical roles. They pioneer new technologies in energy weapons, advanced targeting computers, and neural interfaces. However, this pursuit of perfection has a dark side, leading to morally questionable projects like the 'Apex Prime Candidate Protocol'—an attempt to create the perfect, emotionless soldier.

Life in the Republic is a study in contrasts. Gleaming cityscapes and unparalleled technological comfort exist alongside a rigid social structure and a chilling disregard for individuality. For Horizon, the ends almost always justify the means, and any sacrifice is acceptable in the name of progress and stability.

The betrayal of Lieutenant Akira and Major Kenji was a profound shock to the Republic's system. It represented a failure not of technology, but of control—a variable they could not account for. Their subsequent branding as traitors was swift and absolute, an attempt to erase a dangerous ideological contagion before it could spread.

The 'Apex Frame' is the culmination of the Prime Candidate Protocol—a flawless synthesis of logic and combat potential. It is the Republic's ultimate expression of control, a perfect weapon for a perfect system. To pilot it is to become an extension of the Republic's will, an instrument of its manifest destiny.

factions.name: The Rustfang Clans
factions.description: Scavengers, mechanics, and pit-fighters who thrive in the great scrapheaps of the galaxy.

pages.text: Where others see wastelands of junk, the Rustfang Clans see treasure. These hardy, resourceful clans are the masters of salvage and jury-rigged engineering. Their society is built around the 'Great Scrapyard', a massive artificial moon of debris, and the fighting pits where disputes are settled and legends are made. They value strength, ingenuity, and a good explosion.

Rustfang machines, like the Brawler and the Behemoth, are testaments to their philosophy: bigger is better, and if it ain't broke, add more guns. Their technology is loud, dirty, and surprisingly effective, favoring heavy armor, overwhelming firepower, and brutal melee weapons.

The legends say a world-ending weapon fell from the stars in the old times. The Rustfang found its corpse and built a machine around its still-beating heart. The 'World Eater' is that machine. It is not merely made of scrap; it is the god of scrap, a walking apocalypse that hungers for the ruins of civilizations.

factions.name: The Zenith Concord
factions.description: A mysterious, hyper-advanced faction driven by an inscrutable, alien logic.

pages.text: Little is known about the true origins of the Zenith Concord. They appeared at the edge of known space in silent, geometrically perfect vessels, their motives and biology a complete mystery. They communicate through complex data streams and seem to operate on a level of consciousness far beyond human understanding. They view the chaotic conflicts of humanity with a cold, detached logic, their interventions rare but decisive.

Zenith technology is almost magical in its sophistication. They have mastered gravity manipulation, hard-light projection, and phase technology. Their Warmachines, like the Phalanx and the Singularity, are sleek, silent, and impossibly efficient. It is believed their ultimate goal is not conquest, but 'Correction'—imposing their version of absolute order on a chaotic galaxy.

The machine designated 'Genesis' is not a weapon, but a terraforming tool of immense power. The Concord does not conquer; it corrects. Genesis is the instrument of that correction, capable of rewriting matter and energy at a quantum level. To face it is to face not an army, but the patient, inexorable will of creation itself.

campaigns.name: Mecha Hearts
campaigns.description: Two empires clash, and two pilots find themselves at the center of a war that will change the galaxy.

chapters.title: Chapter 1: Scavenger Hunt
chapters.description: Phoenix Squad moves through an abandoned foundry, hunting scavenger drones and discovering remnants of an unknown, sophisticated technology.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Phoenix Squad, formation Delta-Seven. Main reactor is ahead. Akira has point; hold your spacing and stay out of his crossfire.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: Quiet channel all week, then this foundry starts answering its own drones. I do not like machinery that learns who is listening.

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: I ran the odds on 'adapting drone signals' before we launched. Didn't love the number. Bringing it up anyway, because somebody should.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Copy. We clear the route, scan the core, and get out before this rust heap decides to fall on us.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: This foundry is off the official maps. Drones have been stripping it for weeks, but their signals are adapting. Find out why something is protecting scrap.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Stay sharp. Whatever is in there is not ours, and it is not Aurora's either.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: Contact high-left. Three drones now, with a larger cluster moving around the cooling towers.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: They learned from the first exchange. I will draw them wide. Keep the line and do not let them reach Yuki's flank.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Bulwark has the center. New pilot, cover Akira's retreat. If those cutters breach formation, we lose the corridor.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: On you, Major. Phoenix holds here.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: Whoa. Okay, that alloy signature is NOT scrap-yard standard. I'm reading lattice patterns I've never seen outside a Zenith textbook rumor.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Get a sample and get out. If someone is guarding tech this advanced, they will notice we were here.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: This was not a cleanup run. Whatever made this alloy was here before us.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: And now Phoenix has the evidence. Good work. Do not make me repeat it.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: new op chat! naming rights go to whoever survives the first floor. Yusuke, place your bets now

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: I never bet on outcomes I have not modeled. Give me forty minutes and a whiteboard.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Comms discipline, both of you. This is a live channel, not the mess hall.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: transferred in yesterday and already being told off. good sign, right?

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: Yuki, welcome to Phoenix. Kenji yells at everyone equally. It is load-bearing affection.

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: Whiteboard math says this foundry should not have power. It has power. I do not like when reality skips a step.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: reality skipping steps is my favorite genre, keep us posted nerd

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: first live drone contact and I already lost count past six. is that normal.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: Normal is a floor two problem, Sergeant. Survive floor one first.

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: Revised whiteboard math: whoever wired this place had a maintenance budget nobody signed off on. That is not a scrapyard number.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Keep the math to yourself until we are out, Ensign.

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Brother's Burden
chapters.description: In the Aurora Kingdom, Lieutenant Hikari argues against her younger brother Kaito's premature deployment to the front lines.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: Kaito is SEVENTEEN. He hasn't finished basic neural sync and the Kingdom wants him on the front line for a photo opportunity.

lines.speaker: Ensign Kaito
lines.text: Sister, please. I requested the posting. House Kurenai doesn't hide behind its own walls — you taught me that.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: I taught you duty, not suicide. And now Horizon raiders are hitting this station while we argue about it.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then argue later. Contacts inbound.

lines.speaker: Ensign Kaito
lines.text: See? The mercenary agrees with me! ...That was agreement, right?

lines.speaker: Ensign Kaito
lines.text: Did you see me? Three confirmed kills! Wait until the academy hears—

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: I saw you nearly lose your left flank twice. But... you held. You actually held.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: He fights like you, Lieutenant. Just louder.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: Gods help the Kingdom, he does. Fine, little brother. One deployment. And you fly where I can see you.

lines.speaker: Kaito
lines.text: academy group chat is going WILD that I got a real posting. sending a screenshot the second we are clear

lines.speaker: Hikari
lines.text: You are not screenshotting a live deployment, Kaito. Focus.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Unit-Seven quartermaster wants to know if the "noble house rookie" needs the child-sized cockpit padding.

lines.speaker: Kaito
lines.text: tell the quartermaster I will remember this insult for the rest of my career

lines.speaker: Hikari
lines.text: Unit-Seven, hold the eastern approach. My brother has main effort and I would like him to still have a main effort afterward.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Copy. Eastern approach is ours. He is loud but he is not wrong out there.

lines.speaker: Kaito
lines.text: academy chat has now seen the screenshot. I am a legend. this is the best day of my life

lines.speaker: Hikari
lines.text: You nearly lost a flank twice. It is not the best day of your life, it is the day you got lucky twice.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Both true things can share a day, Lieutenant.

chapters.title: Chapter 3: The First Encounter
chapters.description: In a ruined city, Akira and Hikari, ace pilots of opposing nations, engage in a tense, strategic duel, testing each other's limits.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: Contact report: an Auroran ace is sweeping the ruined city grid. K-Type frame, custom livery. That's Lieutenant Hikari of House Kurenai.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: ...I've seen her flight patterns in the archives. She doesn't fight like a soldier. She fights like a duelist.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: And we're walking into her arena?

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: No. We're walking into her invitation. Stay tight. Watch how she moves — everything she does is a question. Try not to answer wrong.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: OPEN CHANNEL: You fight beautifully, Horizon. It's almost a shame we're at war.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: OPEN CHANNEL: Almost. Your third feint drops your shield arm. Fix it before someone worse than me finds it.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: OPEN CHANNEL: ...Noted. Until next time, then. Bring your best — I'll know if you don't.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Are you two dueling or flirting? Asking for the mission report.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: Log it as reconnaissance.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Taro
lines.text: Channel discipline, Lieutenant. Command frequency isn't for trading compliments with the enemy.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: Yes, Instructor. Old habits — you drilled the banter out of me for three years and it still leaks out under pressure.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Taro
lines.text: Then it's not fixed, it's hidden. Same as that feint he called out. Patience, Hikari. The fight you win by being clever is not the fight you win by being ready. Learn which one this war actually is.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: ...Noted. For real, this time.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: pool is open: does Lieutenant Akira actually fight the Kingdom ace or does he just stare broodingly for twenty minutes

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: I have him staring for six minutes, engaging at minute seven. Odds available.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: This channel is being read by Command. Both of you, cease the wagering.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: noted. taking bets on a SEPARATE, unofficial, definitely-not-this channel

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: Unrelated - border chatter keeps naming a third party. A Liberte gun-for-hire, no flag, no command. Callsign "{{RIVAL_NAME}}".

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: A mercenary with a nickname that fancy either has a great agent or has earned it.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: File it and move on. One more name on a battlefield that already has too many.

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: Update: minute six, still staring. My model is holding. I would like this noted for the record.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: nobody asked for your gloating in advance yusuke

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: Minute seven engagement confirmed. I am framing this whiteboard.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: Akira, your after-action report is due by end of shift. Try to leave "instructive" out of it this time.

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Echoes of Treason
chapters.description: After a brutal ambush, both Akira and Hikari face suspicion from their own commands, who refuse to acknowledge the new threat.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Internal Affairs pulled Akira's flight logs. They think the ambush was leaked from inside Phoenix Squad.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: That ambush wasn't Aurora. The frames were unmarked, the tactics were wrong. Somebody new is playing both sides.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: You know that. I know that. Command prefers the story where it's a traitor they can shoot. So we clear our own names — quietly.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: The evidence trail runs through a Cygnus subsidiary office. Corporate ground. Tread carefully — everything in there is somebody's secret.

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: For the record, I called 'corporate involvement' three weeks ago. Nobody wrote it down. I wrote it down. I have it right here.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: Records secured. The 'leak' originated outside both militaries. Weapons shipments, mercenary contracts... all signed with a red wolf's head.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Red Wolves. I thought they were a scavenger myth mothers scared cadets with.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Myths don't file purchase orders, Major.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: No. They don't. Get this to Akira — and to no one else. Trust just became a luxury.

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: Internal Affairs wants sworn statements from everyone with foundry access. I have already written mine. Twice. For consistency.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: yusuke wrote a SWORN STATEMENT twice for CONSISTENCY. this is why I love this squad

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Both of you, this is a serious inquiry. Somebody inside leaked Akira's logs.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: The evidence trail runs through a Cygnus subsidiary office. Corporate ground - tread carefully.

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: For the record, I flagged "unusual corporate traffic near Phoenix relays" in a report three weeks ago. Nobody read it.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: I am reading it now, Ensign. Send it again.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: okay yusuke gets to be smug about this one, he called it

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: Vindication noted. Filing it next to the whiteboard.

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Aurora's Gilded Cage
chapters.description: Forced to participate in a hollow propaganda parade, Hikari feels the weight of her nation's lies and her secret alliance with Akira.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: A victory parade. Half my wing is barely in the ground and the Kingdom throws me a PARADE for a battle we lost twice as many pilots winning.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Sakura
lines.text: Smile and wave, Lieutenant. That's an order from your best friend, who does not outrank you but is right anyway.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Heads up — perimeter sensors just lit. Someone's using the parade crowd as cover.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: Of course they are. Finally, something honest today. Sakura — get the civilians clear. Mercenary — with me.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Sakura
lines.text: Crowd's safe. And hey — the cameras caught you saving a schoolbus instead of waving. The propaganda office is FURIOUS. It's wonderful.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: Good. Let them choke on something true for once.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: For what it's worth, Lieutenant — the schoolbus was better PR anyway.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: For what it's worth... thank you. Both of you. Today I remembered why I fly.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Sakura
lines.text: parade committee wants Lieutenant Hikari waving with BOTH hands. I told them she only has two and needs one for dignity.

lines.speaker: Hikari
lines.text: I do not have time for the committee's hand-choreography, Sakura.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: For what it is worth, the crowd does not care which hand. They just want to see you.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Sakura
lines.text: see, THAT is the kind of PR instinct I keep asking Command for and never get

lines.speaker: Sergeant Sakura
lines.text: Perimeter sweep flagged three vendors who set up literally this morning. New stalls do not usually smell like ozone.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Good catch. Moving to check now.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Sakura
lines.text: propaganda office wants a statement about the schoolbus. I told them "no comment, she is busy being a hero." they hated that.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Perfect statement. Do not improve it.

chapters.title: Chapter 6: Whispers of the Forgotten
chapters.description: Akira pushes the Ryujin to its limits in a simulation, the strain causing his dangerous "spark" to flare, revealing its toll.

lines.speaker: Ensign Rika Jones
lines.text: Simulation deck is prepped. Lieutenant Akira requested combat parameters at... 140% of rated limits. That can't be right.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: It's right. Something happens when I push past the redline. I need to know what it is before it happens in a real fight.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: And you want a witness who won't file a report.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: I want a witness who'll pull me out if I don't come back. There's a difference. Ready when you are.

lines.speaker: Ensign Rika Jones
lines.text: Vitals are stabilizing. Akira, your neural sync spiked to numbers the machine doesn't have colors for. What WAS that?

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: The spark. When my squad was falling, the machine and I just... became one motion. It felt like drowning in light.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: You were faster than anything I've ever flown with. And you were screaming the entire time. You know that, right?

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: ...No. I didn't. Keep this between us. Please.

lines.speaker: Ensign Rika Jones
lines.text: Simulation deck is prepped. For the record, I asked twice if he was sure about 140%. He was sure twice.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: rika you have been running that sim deck alone for HOURS, come get food when you are done, I saved you the good rations

lines.speaker: Ensign Rika Jones
lines.text: You do not have to keep doing that, Asami.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: yes I do, that is what the good rations are FOR

lines.speaker: Ensign Rika Jones
lines.text: Sync telemetry just did something my instruments do not have a graph for. Building one now.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Keep the recording running. Whatever this is, someone should have proof later.

lines.speaker: Ensign Rika Jones
lines.text: Deck powering down. I am filing this under "classified, ask Akira", which is my professional way of saying I have no idea what I just watched.

chapters.title: Chapter 7: The Unholy Ground
chapters.description: Phoenix Squad is ordered into a third frontal assault on the formidable Fort Delta - a fortress that has already chewed through two divisions before them.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Orders are in. Frontal assault on Fort Delta. Again. Third wave this month.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: That's... that fortress ate two divisions already. Somebody at Command has to know that, right? Right??

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: They know, Asami. They're spending us anyway. Yusuke, you fly rear cover. Rookie — you keep him alive.

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: Rear cover, copy. Statistically the safest slot in the whole formation. I've run the math on it. More than once. It helps.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Understood, Major. Everyone comes home.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Don't make promises this place will make you eat, kid.

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: Can I tell you something stupid, before we hit the next floor?

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: The dog. The one in the photo I carry. It's not mine. Never had a dog — never had a house long enough to keep one alive in, growing up. Found the photo in a supply crate two years back and I just... kept it.

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: I tell everyone it's good luck. That's not really it. I just like knowing that somewhere, some family has a dog that happy to see them come home. I run the numbers on everything else in my life. Never wanted to run them on that. Some things I'd rather just believe are true without checking.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: That's not stupid, Yusuke.

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: Statistically, it's a little stupid. But statistically, so is hope, and everyone still seems to think that one's worth keeping around. So — same policy. I make it home from this one, I'm getting an actual dog. Already decided. No math required.

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: STATIC: Rear guard's holding — more contacts than the brief promised, but the medevac corridor's still open. Ran the numbers on this one too. Didn't like them. Doesn't matter. Corridor stays open.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: Yusuke's frame... I lost his signal on floor four. I kept calling. He didn't... he never...

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: He held the breach so the medevacs could lift. That's the whole report. That's the whole damn report they'll reduce him to.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: I was ten meters away, Kenji. There was nothing left to save. That's on Fort Delta, not on you.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: It's on whoever ordered this. And one day, I'm going to ask them why — with my targeting computer on.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Orders are in. Frontal assault on Fort Delta. Third wave this month.

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: I ran the numbers on this deployment three times. I am not going to share them. Some things are better as a private hobby.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: yusuke that is somehow WORSE than sharing them

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: rear cover with you again, Yusuke. same as last time. try not to make me laugh mid-mission, I need to concentrate.

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: No promises. Comedy is also a coping mechanism. It is in my numbers too.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: yusuke says he is bringing the dog picture again for luck. it is not even his dog. it is a stock photo. he refuses to explain

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: It works. I am not required to explain things that work.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: Rear line holding steady out here. Quieter than the front, for once.

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: Quiet is good. My numbers like quiet.

chapters.title: Chapter 8: The Sunder of Souls
chapters.description: Aurora and Horizon collide again at Fort Delta - and this time, Hikari isn't fighting alone. Her mentor Lt. Taro has his own plan for how this siege ends.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Taro
lines.text: Hold formation, Hikari. Fort Delta doesn't fall to anger. It falls to patience — mine's older than yours.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: Patience is what got the last wave killed, old man. We punch through the western casements or we die in the queue like everyone else.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Taro
lines.text: Ha! There's the student I trained. Fine — your plan, my lead. And if it goes wrong, you fly home and you don't look back. Swear it.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: ...I swear it. Don't make me keep it.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: TARO! No no no — eject, EJECT—

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Taro
lines.text: STATIC: ...frame's done, kid. Reactor's holding just long enough. You taught an old man to hope again. Now keep your damn promise.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Hikari. He's gone. He bought us the corridor — don't waste it. Fly.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: ...Logging final valor citation: Lieutenant Taro, shield of Aurora. I'll keep the promise, old man. I hate you for making me.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Sakura
lines.text: Lieutenant Taro says patience. Lieutenant Hikari says patience got the last wave killed. I say both of you pick a plan before I do it for you.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: For what it is worth, Sakura, they usually land on something workable by the third argument.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Sakura
lines.text: this IS the third argument

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Friendly fire incident on the eastern flank. Sgt. Kim is not responding.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: kenji that grid was OURS, how does friendly fire happen on OUR grid

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: I am pulling the logs myself, Ensign. Nobody speculates until I have an answer.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: A coordinate error at that range is a one-in-thousands event, Major. Check the relay chain, not just the gunner. Yusuke would have said the same thing.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Sakura
lines.text: The western casements are quiet now. Whatever happened up there, Lieutenant Hikari is not answering hails.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: give her time sakura. some things you do not push.

chapters.title: Interlude: The Great Frog Crate Incident
chapters.description: A quiet supply depot turns out to be infested with Frog Crates - spring-loaded loot pods that grew legs, feelings, and an attitude. For one afternoon, Phoenix Squad gets to fight something that can't actually hurt them.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: Requisition Depot Theta-Nine stopped answering hails. Thermal's picking up multiple contacts — bipedal, low mass, barely worth flagging as a threat. And the gait pattern... my board keeps calling it 'hopping.'

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Hopping. Command is scrambling Phoenix Squad after something that hops.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: Major, look at the feed! Those are SUPPLY CRATES! With little legs! And the lid-flip they keep doing is one hundred percent sass!

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: I haven't laughed at a briefing in weeks. I'll take this fight. I want the sassy one.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: For the record: strangest sentence I've ever said in this cockpit. We're deploying against loot crates. Let's go meet the Frog Crates.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: Lieutenant, you've been staring at that one for two whole minutes. He's not going to combo you. I checked. He mostly headbutts ankles.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: He keeps trying to close his own lid and hide inside it. Backwards logic. I respect it. ...I'm calling him Norio.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Focus, Lieutenant. Also — did you just name a hostile combatant Norio?

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: He looked like a Norio. Yusuke would have named him something worse.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Depot's secured. No casualties, no meaningful property damage, and one Frog Crate currently welded to Lieutenant Akira's boot.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: Norio is coming with us. That's not a request.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: The terror of two empires, smuggling a loot crate onto a Horizon warship. I am framing this memory forever.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: Thank you for this, Major. I needed a day where nothing we loved got hurt.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Enjoy it while it lasts, Phoenix. Command's already forwarding the Fort Delta inquiry transcripts. Tomorrow we go back to being blamed for surviving. Today, we had a good day.

chapters.title: Chapter 9: Ashes and Accusations
chapters.description: In the aftermath of the disastrous Fort Delta campaign, both Akira and Hikari are blamed by their commands, further cementing their secret alliance.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: Board of Inquiry findings: 'pilot error and insufficient aggression.' They blamed the dead, and then they blamed Akira.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Two armies, one script. Aurora's board pinned their losses on Hikari the same hour. Almost like someone wrote both reports.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Someone did. The question is where they're sitting.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: Then we stop asking permission to find out. Hikari's willing to trade intel. Tonight. If anyone here objects... forget you heard this.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Heard what? Move out.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: You're late.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: I had to lose an actual tail this time, not a metaphorical one. You should be flattered.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: I am. Terrified, but flattered.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: Good. Terrified is the correct amount, given what I'm risking to be standing in this particular hallway. Now — what does your board actually know?

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: You'd never walk away from this. You like it too much.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: The intelligence-sharing, or the company?

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: ...Ask me again when this war's over.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Sakura
lines.text: So let me get this straight, Lieutenant: your secret contact in Horizon is the same ace you keep 'coincidentally' dueling. THE Akira.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: It's an intelligence arrangement, Sakura.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Sakura
lines.text: Uh-huh. And I'm the Queen of the Kingdom. Relax — your secret's safe. Just... be careful which war you end up fighting for.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: She's right. Both commands smell blood now. From here on, every friend is a risk.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: Board of Inquiry findings just hit every terminal in the sector. I compared Horizon's report to Aurora's. Same sentence structure. Same three adjectives. That is not a coincidence, that is a template.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: you compared their PROSE STYLE? nakamura that is the most yusuke thing you have ever done

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: ...Somebody on this squad has to keep the habit alive, Ensign.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: And this time the habit is useful. Write it up properly and get it to Akira.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: is it just me or does everyone on this channel suddenly sound like they are choosing words very carefully

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: yuki honey that is just Tuesday now, welcome to Phoenix Squad politics

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: Follow-up on "{{RIVAL_NAME}}" - Command quietly offered a bounty for Akira. The offer came back marked refused, in writing.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: A mercenary who turns down money. Now that is a rumor worth repeating.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: a bounty on our own ace and the only one with standards is the freelancer. what a war.

chapters.title: Chapter 10: The Hangar Ballad
chapters.description: On administrative leave, Akira finds a moment of unexpected peace watching Ensign Asami's joyful, defiant dance in the hangar.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: Administrative leave means the hangar is OURS! No drills, no alarms, just me, a sound rig, and three days of choreography I've been saving.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: You want to dance. In a war zone. Between the ammunition racks.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: I want to dance BECAUSE it's a war zone, dummy. If we stop being people, what's even left to defend? Now sit. Watch. Both of you. Front row.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: You heard the Ensign. Sit down, Lieutenant. Some orders you don't fight.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: ...I haven't heard music in two years. I kept combat-scanning the room for the first minute. And then I just... didn't.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: That's called being alive, Lieutenant! It looks good on you. Don't let it be another two years before you try it again.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: When this war ends, Asami, you'll fill stadiums.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: When this war ends, you're ALL getting front-row seats. That's a promise. Asami never breaks a promise!

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: administrative leave means the hangar is OURS. sound rig is borrowed, do not ask from where, the answer involves a promise I intend to keep quietly

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: is Lieutenant Akira actually going to sit through this or bail after five minutes

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: he will stay. yusuke had a whole theory about it. I am choosing to trust the theory.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: then today we test it. for science. and for yusuke.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: he is still here. the theory holds.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: of course it holds. that dork never wrote down a number he was not sure about.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: HE STAYED FOR THE WHOLE THING. somewhere out there a whiteboard is vindicated

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: front row seats and a proven theory. good day. rare kind.

chapters.title: Chapter 11: The Naval Gambit
chapters.description: A massive naval battle erupts at Aurora Harbor. Veteran pilot Lt. Yamamoto has been quiet all briefing - and everyone's about to find out why.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Yamamoto
lines.text: Aurora Harbor. I did my first tour here, twenty years ago. Prettiest water in the sector — you'd never know from up here today.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: You've been quiet all briefing, Yamamoto. What aren't you saying?

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Yamamoto
lines.text: That I left a family behind to fly these things, and I never once told them why. Old men get talkative before big battles. Ignore me.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Enemy fleet on the horizon. All wings — this one's going to hurt. Fly like your wingman's life depends on it, because it does.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Yamamoto
lines.text: STATIC: —missile spread's through, I'm the only angle. Kenji, tell my daughter... tell her the money was never the reason. The reason was she gets to grow old.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Yamamoto, break off. BREAK OFF. That's an order—

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Yamamoto
lines.text: STATIC: First order I ever ignored. Been an honor, Phoenix.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: ...Impact confirmed. The carrier's gone. He took it with him.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Log it. Then fly. We mourn on the ground — that's the deal. That's always been the deal.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Yamamoto
lines.text: Aurora Harbor. First tour I ever flew was right here, twenty years back. Funny what stays the same and what does not.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: twenty years, sir? were the fish worth writing home about at least

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Yamamoto
lines.text: Never once caught one. Kept going back anyway. That is most of what you need to know about me, Sergeant.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: when this is over we are all going fishing and NOBODY is allowed to bring a rifle

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: is it me or did Lieutenant Yamamoto sound like he was saying goodbye back there

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: do not think like that yuki. he is a twenty year veteran, he has said goodbye a hundred times and come back a hundred times

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: Carrier signature just dropped off every board at once. I have no readout for what that means and I am not going to guess on an open channel.

chapters.title: Chapter 12: Whispers of the Third Path
chapters.description: Akira and Hikari exchange intel on the Red Wolves and their own deteriorating physical and mental states, leading them to the reclusive Professor Fujimoto.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: You plan for eleven contingencies before breakfast. I plan for none and I'm still alive. Explain that.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: Luck isn't a plan, Hikari.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: No, it's a personality. Yours could use one.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: Your hands were shaking on the approach vector. Don't tell me it's the cold, Akira. Mine started last month.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: Sync degradation. The harder we fly, the worse it gets. Whatever our machines are doing to us, it's the same thing on both sides of this war.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Which means it's not a malfunction. It's a design.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: There's one man who'd know. Professor Fujimoto — the architect of the neural interface. He vanished eight years ago. We found him.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: Then let's go ask the good professor what he built us into.

lines.speaker: Professor Fujimoto
lines.text: Go away. I don't consult, I don't repent, and I certainly don't help pilots who are already... oh. Oh no. Your eyes. Both of you. How long have you had the tremors?

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: Months. You recognize it. WHAT is it?

lines.speaker: Professor Fujimoto
lines.text: My greatest work, coming home to roost. Come inside. Quickly. And you — the mercenary — watch the door. What I'm about to say has killed everyone who's heard it.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Door's covered. Talk fast, Professor.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: Yamamoto's locker is still packed for a tour he is not coming back from. Command asked if anyone wants to sort it. Nobody has volunteered. Understandably.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: I will do it. Someone should, and it should be someone who liked him, not a stranger with a clipboard.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: there is a photo of a girl in his flight jacket pocket. I think that is his daughter. I did not open it, I just saw the corner.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: Send it to Command sealed, Sergeant. Some things do not belong in an inventory log.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: Squad rumor mill says Fujimoto is some kind of hermit genius who vanished eight years ago. In my experience "vanished" usually means "made to disappear." I would like to be wrong.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: whatever the professor told Akira and Hikari in there, they came out looking like they aged five years. nobody is talking about it

chapters.title: Chapter 13: The Calm Before the Storm
chapters.description: At a fragile peace conference, Asami gives a heartfelt performance. Akira and Hikari share a dance, a silent truce that culminates in a desperate kiss.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: A real peace conference! With delegates! And they asked ME to perform! Okay, technically I volunteered. Loudly. Until they said yes.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Sakura
lines.text: Half the guns in the galaxy are in this room wearing dress uniforms. Some peace.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then let's make it real for one night. Asami — stage is yours.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: One night is all I need! Hey, Lieutenant Akira — the Auroran ace keeps looking at you. You should ask her to dance before the song's over. Life's short!

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: You dance worse than you duel, Horizon.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: You lead in both. I've stopped fighting it.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: Akira... when the music stops, we go back to being enemies. So don't let it stop yet.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: PRIVATE CHANNEL: Perimeter's quiet. Whatever this is between them... let them have tonight. Everyone deserves one night.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: A REAL PEACE CONFERENCE. with a REAL STAGE. I already picked the setlist, do not test me on this

lines.speaker: Sergeant Sakura
lines.text: the seating chart puts two admirals who tried to assassinate each other at the same table. whoever arranged that is either a genius or a comedian.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: either way they get an encore, sakura. ESPECIALLY them

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: Perimeter sweep flagged an unregistered escort frame shadowing the Liberte delegation. Callsign on the transponder: "{{RIVAL_NAME}}".

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: The mystery mercenary is working peace conference security. Of all the odd jobs.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Sakura
lines.text: Liberte hired the one gun they know will not sell them out. Leave the escort be.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Sakura
lines.text: protocol office asked me to keep Lieutenant Hikari away from the Horizon delegation table tonight. I told them absolutely not and also mind their own business.

chapters.title: Chapter 14: When the Music Died
chapters.description: The Red Wolves shatter the fragile peace conference mid-performance. In the chaos, Hikari loses sight of everyone she came here to protect.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: —breach in the east hall! They're not delegates, they're wolves, ACTUAL Red Wolves, somebody get the civilians—

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Asami, fall back to the hangar, that is a DIRECT order—

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: Can't, Major! There are kids in the green room and I'm the only one who knows the way out! It's okay. It's okay. I never break a promise, remember?

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Asami, wait for me, I'm thirty seconds out — ASAMI—

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: The children made it out. All twelve. She was three meters from the door.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: In the chaos — my brother. Aurora's own secret police took Kaito. Not the Wolves. OURS. What is HAPPENING to this galaxy?

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: War stopped being between nations tonight. Whoever did this... we find them. For Asami. Front-row seats — we all still owe her that.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: five minutes to stage time and I am somehow MORE nervous than any mission. this is a whole different muscle

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: you have rehearsed through three walls for a week, asami. the set is going to be great. I have witnesses. the walls are witnesses.

lines.speaker: Ensign Asami
lines.text: yuki that is either the sweetest or most backhanded thing you have said to me and I am choosing sweet

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: something feels wrong in the east hall. probably nothing. probably just nerves. probably.

chapters.title: Chapter 15: Forging the Treacherous Bond
chapters.description: Publicly blaming each other for the Citadel attack, Akira and Hikari secretly establish a new, deeper line of communication to find the truth.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: The official line: Akira and Hikari blame each other for the Citadel attack. The press releases practically write themselves.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: Good. Let both commands watch us snarl at each other on every broadcast. Meanwhile — new channel, triple-encrypted, dead-drop relays.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: You two are now officially the galaxy's worst enemies and only allies. Try not to laugh on the broadcast — it'll ruin the performance.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: RELAY: When this is over, mercenary, you can write the memoirs. Chapter one: everyone lied. Now — a Cygnus 'observer' wants to meet. Watch them closely.

lines.speaker: "Observer"
lines.text: Cygnus Corporation extends its... condolences on recent events. We offer logistics, intelligence, and discretion. In exchange: combat telemetry. Nothing more.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: And what does a corporation want with the combat data of two disgraced aces?

lines.speaker: "Observer"
lines.text: Everything, eventually. But today? Merely to watch. You are the most interesting variables in the sector, and Cygnus dislikes being surprised.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: RELAY: We take the deal. Eyes open. A knife you can see is still better than one you can't.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Confirmation from medical came through this morning. Ensign Asami is gone.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: Her last upload was the setlist from that night. I am archiving it on this channel. Nobody deletes it. Ever.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: she saved me the good rations every single week since I transferred in. I did not even like her at first. I liked her by the second week. everyone did, by the second week.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: For the record: a Cygnus courier drone delivered a case of restoration-grade sound equipment to the memorial hangar this morning. No invoice. No note.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: the corporation that watches everything sent flowers the only way it knows how. I do not know what to do with that.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Log it and keep both eyes open. Kindness with no invoice is just an invoice you have not seen yet.

chapters.title: Chapter 16: The Architect's Guilt
chapters.description: Professor Fujimoto finally agrees to talk - and what he's spent years trying to forget may explain everything happening to Akira, and to Kaito.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: If Fujimoto says what I think he's about to say, I need you to not look at me differently afterward.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: I've watched you eat cold ration paste and call it 'fine.' There's no version of you left that could still surprise me.

lines.speaker: Professor Fujimoto
lines.text: Sit down. Both of you. What I'm about to say, I've rehearsed for eight years and it still tastes like poison.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: The spark. Tell me what it is.

lines.speaker: Professor Fujimoto
lines.text: It's called the Apex Project. A hive-mind protocol. Your 'talent' is a leash, Akira — you were engineered to one day stop being a pilot and start being a NODE.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: And Kaito? WHERE IS MY BROTHER?

lines.speaker: Professor Fujimoto
lines.text: Aurora's mirror program. The Oni. I'm sorry, Lieutenant. They didn't arrest him. They harvested him.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Professor — data's secure, extraction's clear. You just burned every bridge you had left. Why now?

lines.speaker: Professor Fujimoto
lines.text: Because I built the cage, mercenary. Every night for eight years I dreamed of the children who'd grow up to be locked in it. Then two of them knocked on my door.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: You can't unbuild it?

lines.speaker: Professor Fujimoto
lines.text: No. But I can build the key. Get me materials, time, and protection — and I will end the age of Warmachines myself.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: Fujimoto has been in that room with Akira and Hikari for three hours. Nobody has come out. Nobody has asked to.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: three hours. whatever takes three hours to say is not going to fit in a report field.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: Akira came out first. Did not say a word. Hikari came out an hour later. Also did not say a word. I do not think either of them slept.

chapters.title: Chapter 17: The Ghost's Shadow
chapters.description: Pursuing their first mission together, Akira and Hikari are ambushed by a silent, perfect prototype—a ghost they cannot defeat.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: First mission as actual partners. Feels wrong flying with your IFF showing green, Horizon.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: Feels right to me. That's what worries me. Sensor contact — something's shadowing us through the industrial stacks.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: I've got no signature, no exhaust plume, no sync noise. Whatever's out there flies cleaner than anything human.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: Perfect flight discipline. Zero hesitation. That's not a pilot. That's what Fujimoto warned us we'd become. Weapons free — and stay ALIVE.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: We didn't beat it. Understand that. It flew through the three of us like weather and then it simply... chose to leave.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: It matched every maneuver you made before you made it, Hikari. Like it had studied you your whole life.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: ...Why does that sentence make my blood run cold?

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: Because somewhere behind that ghost's eyes, something recognized US too. We need Kingu. The Wolves' strategist knows who's building these. We take him alive.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: PRIVATE CHANNEL: When it went for you first, I stopped thinking like a soldier. That should worry me more than it does.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: PRIVATE CHANNEL: It should worry both of us. I keep telling myself this is strategy. Tonight I believed that for almost a whole minute.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: PRIVATE CHANNEL: And the other fifty-nine seconds?

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: PRIVATE CHANNEL: Don't make me say it over an open channel, Horizon. Some things I'm not ready to lose to a war yet.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: First joint patrol log with Aurora on it since this war started. My paperwork template does not have a field for "enemy IFF, now green." I am improvising one.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: a year ago I trained to shoot that exact paint scheme. today it is covering my flank. nobody at the academy has a class for this.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: Unconnected note: three Red Wolves supply convoys hit in the last week, all quietly, all professionally. Same signature both times: "{{RIVAL_NAME}}".

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: whoever they are, they are fighting our war without waiting to be asked.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: Whatever flew through that formation did not register on a single sensor suite in this squadron. I have nothing to file. I am filing that fact itself.

chapters.title: Chapter 18: Unmasking the Puppeteer
chapters.description: In a daring stealth mission, the team captures the Red Wolves' strategist, Kingu - and gets far more than the intel they came for.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Kingu. The Red Wolves' pet strategist. Every ambush that's bled us for two years has his fingerprints on the timing.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Mine complex, skeleton garrison, one very smug target in the command module. It's almost too clean.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: It's exactly too clean. Which is why you're going in quiet and I'm staying loud out here. Anything smells wrong, you abort. Kid — I mean it.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: Everything about this war smells wrong, Major. Quiet as we can. Let's meet the puppeteer.

lines.speaker: Matsuo
lines.text: BROADCAST: Congratulations on capturing my strategist! One small detail: Kingu has been ours AND yours the entire time. Check your own command frequencies — they already know where you sleep.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: A double agent. He let us take him. The capture WAS the message.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: So both our commands now have proof the two of you are working together. That was the trap. Not the mine — the truth.

lines.speaker: Matsuo
lines.text: BROADCAST: The mercenary understands! I like that one. Run along, little heroes. The interesting part starts now.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: Wait — before you cut the channel. Why any of this? Why the Wolves?

lines.speaker: Matsuo
lines.text: BROADCAST: ...You want the speech? Fine, heiress. Once. I was born in a border district both empires claimed on paper and starved in practice. Zero schools, zero clinics, two tax collectors arguing over which crown owed my mother medicine. Both said the other. Both were right. That is the punchline of your entire system — everyone is responsible, so no one is.

lines.speaker: Matsuo
lines.text: BROADCAST: So I built something that does not argue jurisdiction. The Wolves do not ask which flag starved you. We just make the ones who did it go a little hungry too, and we sign our own name to the hunger.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: That's not government, Matsuo. That's a body count with a flag stapled to it.

lines.speaker: Matsuo
lines.text: BROADCAST: Every government is, mercenary. You want the real difference between my empire and theirs? Mine tells you exactly whose blood built it. Go look at your own banners, little heroes, and tell me yours has the courage to do the same.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: the mine schematics list a wine cellar. a WINE CELLAR. in a forward operating base. who is this strategist

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: A man who has never once expected to be raided, Sergeant. Which is either confidence or information. Assume the second.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: Garrison was lighter than intel projected. Either our numbers were wrong or someone wanted us to get this far easily.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: when has this war ever handed us anything easily. keep your guns warm.

chapters.title: Chapter 19: Cracks in the Facade
chapters.description: The intel pulled from Kingu doesn't add up - and the deeper Akira and Hikari dig, the less either side's official story survives contact with the truth.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: I've decrypted Kingu's archive three times because I refused to believe it twice. Horizon and Aurora high command are collaborating. The war is managed.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: Managed. Taro died for a QUOTA. Asami died for a spreadsheet's margin of error.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: The Red Wolves are the pressure valve — funded by both crowns to keep the fear alive, so the Apex and Oni programs keep their funding.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then there are no sides left to be loyal to. Just people. Everyone still in this room — that's the whole army now.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Smallest army I've ever served in. Best one, too.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: Corporate registry confirms it. Shell companies feeding both programs, all clearing through Cygnus banks. Our 'Observer' friend has been invoicing the apocalypse.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: And they'll sell us the rope to hang their clients with, if the telemetry's good. Corporations don't have sides, just ledgers.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: Then we use the ledger. Every shipment has a route. Every route has a source. Follow the money far enough...

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: ...and we find the room where they decided our lives were a rounding error. I want to stand in that room.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: The archive matches the inquiry reports. Same template, same three adjectives, same author fingerprints. The theory I would not say out loud in chapter four is now a finding.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: I gave thirty years to this uniform. Tonight I learned what it was actually buying.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: is everyone else as angry as I am right now or is that just me

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Not just you. Hold onto it. Angry means we still expect better - the day we stop being angry is the day they win.

chapters.title: Chapter 20: The Great Betrayal
chapters.description: A tip from inside Phoenix Squad leads Akira, Hikari, and Kenji straight into an ambush - and straight into being branded traitors by the allies they trusted.

lines.speaker: Ensign Rika Jones
lines.text: The informant confirmed it — defectors from the Oni program, hiding at the old comms array. They'll only meet tonight. Only you three.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Rika, you're sure about the source? One bad coordinate out here and we're meat in a box.

lines.speaker: Ensign Rika Jones
lines.text: I verified everything myself, Major. ...Akira. Whatever happens tonight — I want you to know I always watched you. Always.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: That's... an odd way to say good luck, Rika.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Contacts on all vectors — those are OUR squadrons' idents! It's a trap — RIKA?!

lines.speaker: Ensign Rika Jones
lines.text: BROADCAST: They promised me you'd survive it, Akira. They promised they just wanted the three of you contained. I'm sorry. I couldn't watch you destroy yourself chasing this—

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: You sold us to the people who built the cage, Rika. Because you LOVED me? Look at what that word means to you.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Save it. We're branded traitors on every channel in two empires. Extraction NOW — grieve at cruising speed.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Three armies hunting us and nowhere to land. So — where does the galaxy's most wanted squad go from here?

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Down, kid. We go underground. And then we dig up the truth by the roots.

lines.speaker: Ensign Rika Jones
lines.text: Route package for tonight is on your terminals. I triple-checked the approach lanes myself. Fly them exactly, please. Exactly.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: rika you okay? you have checked that package four times in an hour

lines.speaker: Ensign Rika Jones
lines.text: I am fine. I just want tonight to go the way it is supposed to. That is all I have ever wanted for him. For all of you. For everyone.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: our own squadron idents on the attack vectors. OURS. I trained with some of those callsigns.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Grieve at cruising speed, Sergeant. Every second we spend feeling this is a second they gain on us.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: One more thing off tonight's wreckage - an extraction beacon on the comms array, signed only "{{RIVAL_NAME}}". It opened our escape corridor before we asked for one.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: a stranger saved us tonight and a friend sold us. I am going to need a while with that one.

chapters.title: Chapter 21: Revelation and Despair
chapters.description: Hiding in the ruins, Fujimoto finally tells them everything he knows about the Ghost, and about what Akira was always meant to become. Neither of them walks away from that conversation the same.

lines.speaker: Professor Fujimoto
lines.text: Stop pacing, all of you. If we're going to die in a ruin, we might as well die informed. There's one more file. The deepest one. I need you sitting down, Akira.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: I've run out of ways to be broken, Professor. Say it standing.

lines.speaker: Professor Fujimoto
lines.text: The Ghost that outflew you — its designation is Oni-Prime. Its donor subject was Ensign Kaito Kurenai. Hikari... the Ghost is your brother.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: No. No, we FOUGHT it — I shot at — I shot at my own—

lines.speaker: Professor Fujimoto
lines.text: And Akira. The Apex files name their Prime Candidate Alpha. It has always been you. Both programs were built around the two of you meeting.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Akira's locked himself in the maintenance bay. He's been staring at his own hands for six hours. I've seen combat breaks before. This is worse.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: His whole life just became someone else's blueprint, Kenji. Every victory, every instinct — designed. You don't walk that off.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: Then we don't let him carry it alone. Open the bay door, Major. My brother is a weapon and the man I love is a blueprint — and I am DONE letting their designers write one more line of our story.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: ...Opening the door. Gods help whoever's on the other side of that woman.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: ...I don't know which parts of me are mine anymore, Hikari.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: The instinct that's saved this squad a dozen times — designed. The reflexes Command called a gift — designed. Maybe even the part of me that wanted to protect people in the first place. I can't tell anymore if that was a boy's choice, or a specification.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: Then find the part that isn't. I'll wait as long as it takes.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: ...This. Wanting to walk out that door because you're the one standing on the other side of it. Nobody designed that into me. I checked. I checked twice, because I needed it to be true.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: So if there's one honest thing left in me, it's this: built or born, designed or free, I would choose you in every version of me they ever could have made. That much, at least, is mine. That much they never got to touch.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: we have been branded traitors on two flags in one week. is there a support group for this. asking for myself

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: There is not, Sergeant. I checked. If we survive the month I will draft a charter.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: the bay door has been shut for six hours. does anyone bring him food? water? do we knock? somebody tell me what the protocol is for THIS

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: There is no protocol, Yuki. There is just waiting with the door in sight so he knows someone is on the other side of it.

chapters.title: Chapter 22: The Struggle for Sanity
chapters.description: Hunted by the Oni-Kaito, Hikari must appeal to her brother's lost humanity while Akira fights the final activation of the Apex protocol in his own mind.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: It's getting louder. The protocol. It has a VOICE now — it sounds like me, but patient. It keeps offering to take the pain away.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: And what do you tell it?

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: That pain is the only proof I'm still the one flying. Contact alarm — that's Oni-Prime's signature. Kaito found us.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: Then today I stop fighting the Ghost and start fighting FOR my brother. Keep the escorts off me. Whatever you hear on this channel — do not interfere.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: KAITO! Three months before the academy — you broke mother's telescope and blamed the gardener's cat! NOBODY else knows that! The machine doesn't know that! YOU do!

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: Its flight pattern is fracturing... it pulled the killing blow. Hikari, it PULLED the blow—

lines.speaker: Ensign Kaito
lines.text: STATIC: ...hikari...? sister, it's so dark in here—

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Signal's cut. It's retreating — no, it's FLEEING. She reached him. There's still a boy inside that ghost.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: Hikari said not to interfere on this channel no matter what we hear. So we are not going to. Copy that, everyone. copy it twice.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: Escorts on us, guns off her channel. Whatever family business happens out there today, it happens between the two of them.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: Whatever just happened out there, the Oni unit broke off mid-engagement. That does not happen. Something changed.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: I am choosing to read that as good news and I am not going to poke it. some things you just let be true.

chapters.title: Chapter 23: Sacrifice and Echoes
chapters.description: Hikari makes one last attempt to reach the brother buried inside the Ghost. Whatever happens next, the Oni Program's command vessel will not survive it.

lines.speaker: Ensign Kaito
lines.text: OPEN CHANNEL: Sister. I don't have long — the conditioning reasserts in cycles. The command vessel controls every Oni frame. I know its blind spot. I AM its blind spot.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: Kaito, we'll extract you. Fujimoto can undo it, we'll find a way, we ALWAYS—

lines.speaker: Ensign Kaito
lines.text: There's no undoing, Hikari. But there's one thing the boy you raised can still choose. Let me choose it. Fly with me. One last time. Like the station — you and me against the world.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Escort formation on the kid. Everyone — we punch him a corridor and we DON'T look back.

lines.speaker: Ensign Kaito
lines.text: STATIC: Corridor's clear. Reactor overload in ten. Hey, sister? You were wrong at the station — House Kurenai doesn't hide behind walls... it BECOMES one. Tell your ace to take care of you.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: Kaito— KAITO—

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: ...Someone gave the order that put my brother in that machine. I want a name, Akira. I want a name, and I want them to see me coming.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: Command vessel is gone. Every Oni frame in the sector just went dark. He freed all of them, Hikari. Every child they took.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: ...He held. My little brother held. Log it under valor, mercenary. Log it under the brightest thing this war ever burned.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: escort formation locked in on the kid. everybody hold your lane no matter what.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: Corridor plot is as clean as I can make it. The rest is his. Give him a straight road.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: Every Oni frame in the sector just went dark simultaneously. Whatever happened up there, it was not small.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: nobody on this channel has said anything in twenty minutes. I do not think anyone knows what to say.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then we do not say anything tonight. Some things deserve the quiet.

chapters.title: Chapter 24: The Point of No Return
chapters.description: With their enemies closing in, the team makes a final, agonizing decision: to deploy Fujimoto's EMP, a choice that will silence all machines.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: Before the briefing — the freed Oni transports finished decrypting overnight. Subject H-117, recovered alive: Ensign Yusuke, Phoenix Squad. He's thin, he's half-starved... and he's asking for his whiteboard.

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: STATIC: This channel still open? Somebody tell the Major the odds of me making this call were terrible. I made it anyway. Turns out that's kind of my thing.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: ...Yusuke. You held that breach. We wrote the report. We MOURNED you, kid.

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: Aurora pulled me out of the wreck before the fire finished the job. I spent a year as spare parts for the Oni program — then every cell door on that ship opened at once. Kaito's doing. I owe a dead kid a debt I can't pay back, so I'm here to pay it forward. Put me on the roster, Major.

lines.speaker: Professor Fujimoto
lines.text: The EMP is finished. One pulse through the Aetherium Conduit and every neural-linked machine in the sector goes silent. Forever. Including... everything you fly.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: You're asking career pilots to kill every machine they've ever loved. Including the ones keeping us alive right now.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: He's asking us to end the war, Kenji. All of it. The programs, the Wolves, the managed slaughter — no machines, no Warmachine war.
