lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: And no Apex protocol. No more children built into weapons. I vote yes.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: For Kaito. For Asami. For Taro. Yes. May the gods forgive us — the historians certainly won't.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Supplies secured, route to the Conduit mapped. Last chance to walk away, kid. Nobody would blame a mercenary for skipping the apocalypse.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: You're the only family I've got left in this galaxy, Major. Somebody has to fly rear cover for the end of the world.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Ha. Yusuke used to say that. All right, Phoenix Squad — final approach starts at dawn. Get some sleep. Tomorrow we make history or we make craters.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: Decrypted manifests from the freed Oni transports finished processing overnight. Subject H-117, recovered alive: Ensign Yusuke, Phoenix Squad. I have read the line forty times. It does not stop being true.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: WHAT

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: Hi, everyone. Reports of my death were... statistically reasonable, honestly. I would have believed them too.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: I called your signal for an HOUR, yusuke. an HOUR. you are never allowed to go dark again. squad rule. new charter. I am drafting it

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: Accepted without reading the terms. Also: someone kept my whiteboard theory alive while I was gone. I noticed. Thank you. You know who you are.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: last chance to walk away, Kenji said. nobody on this channel is walking away. just so that is on the record.

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: Recorded. I spent a year in a cell the size of a cockpit because this war needed spare parts. There was never a version of me that walks away from ending it.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: A back-channel offer reached Fujimoto's relay overnight - unsigned help evacuating the outposts before the EMP fires. Same handle again: "{{RIVAL_NAME}}".

lines.speaker: Professor Fujimoto
lines.text: I did not ask. I do not care. Send them every evacuation route we have.

chapters.title: Chapter 25: The Mirror's Shattering
chapters.description: The EMP fails to stop Tiamat's modified Bahamut. Akira must consciously use the Apex conditioning, embracing the monster within to win.

lines.speaker: Tiamat
lines.text: BROADCAST: Little birds, little birds, flying to pull the plug on the whole beautiful bonfire! Tiamat says NO. Tiamat's Bahamut ate your little pulse for BREAKFAST.

lines.speaker: Professor Fujimoto
lines.text: Impossible — the prototype EMP discharge was direct, her frame should be DEAD—

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: Modified shielding. Matsuo knew about the pulse. There's only one thing on this battlefield faster than that monster... and it's the monster in my head.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Akira, if you open that door, can you close it again?

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: Ask me after. Hikari — if I come back wrong... you know what I need you to do.

lines.speaker: Tiamat
lines.text: STATIC: hahaha... HAHAHA! There you are! THERE'S the real one! Finally somebody FUN — again! AGAIN—

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: Her frame's down. Akira, it's over. Akira. AKIRA. Look at me. Come back. Come BACK.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: ...I'm here. I'm still here. I used it and I'm still ME. It's screaming about it, but I'm still me.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then that's the weapon they never planned for — a Prime who won't stop being a person. Let's go break their conduit.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: Tiamat is still flying after a direct EMP hit. I do not understand the physics and I do not want to.

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: Neither do I, and physics is usually my whole personality. I am unsettled on a professional level.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: Akira went dark on this channel the moment he engaged her. He is back now. Whatever that cost him, he paid it and came back.

chapters.title: Chapter 26: The Storm of Revelation
chapters.description: The final push. The team fights their way to the Aetherium Conduit to deploy the EMP, with the Red Wolves leader Matsuo standing in their way.

lines.speaker: Matsuo
lines.text: BROADCAST: And so the children arrive at the summit of the world. Do you know why I let the empires fund my Wolves? Because rot deserves a match, and they kept HANDING me matches.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: You killed Asami. You broke the peace. You fed two nations to each other and called it philosophy.

lines.speaker: Matsuo
lines.text: BROADCAST: I ACCELERATED the inevitable, little heiress. Your EMP and I want the same dead machines — I simply want to be standing on top when they fall. Come. The mountain awaits.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Talk's over, Matsuo. Phoenix Squad — final climb. Everything we've lost is watching.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Conduit chamber's ahead. Matsuo's personal guard is dust. All that's left is the man himself... and he's waiting at the trigger like he OWNS it.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: He wants the pulse fired on his terms, with him as the last god of the old world. He doesn't get to have it.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: Together, then. All of us, one door, no more secrets on the other side.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: For the record — best squad I ever flew with. Now let's go end an age.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Final approach to the Aetherium Conduit. Matsuo and the last Red Wolves hold the pass.

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: I ran survival odds for this climb about six different ways. I am not sharing the number. Some things you climb anyway.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: good. do not share it. some of us would like to keep climbing without knowing.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: A lone white frame just carved a hole clean through the Red Wolves' rear line. No orders, no request for a share of the credit. Same handle: "{{RIVAL_NAME}}".

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: That is the whole list now. Every entry under "things I cannot explain but am grateful for" has the same signature. I would like to meet them. Properly, not through a sensor log.

chapters.title: Chapter 27: The Silent Fall
chapters.description: To end this, Akira has to go further into the Apex protocol than anyone ever has - and there's no guarantee of what comes back out.

lines.speaker: Matsuo
lines.text: The Fenrir and I have eaten a hundred aces. But you didn't come to duel, did you, Prime Candidate? You came to become. I can SEE it behind your eyes, straining at the leash.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: The EMP needs a neural key — a mind fully merged with the machine network. It was always going to be me. It was DESIGNED to be me.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: Akira, no — we find another way, we ALWAYS find another—

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: Not this time, love. Beat him with me. Then let me go be the key. And Hikari — whatever walks back out of that light... be patient with it. Some of me will still be in there.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: The pulse... it's spreading like a sunrise. Every machine in the sector going quiet, one by one. It's almost gentle.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: Matsuo's frame is dead metal. The war machines are dead metal. And Akira is standing in the middle of it, breathing. Akira...?

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Matsuo's cockpit read three seconds of life signs after the pulse hit — then nothing. Whatever he was trying to become when that light took him, he didn't get to finish it.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then that's the whole obituary he gets. Not a martyr. Not a god. Just a man who ran out of matches to hand people.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: ...The network is silent. The voice is silent. Everything is so... quiet. Hikari. I remember the telescope story. I remember the dance. I'm keeping those.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: Then that's enough to rebuild from. Come home, Akira. Come home slowly, and I'll be there for every step.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: Matsuo is still talking. Somebody tell him the debate portion of this war ended chapters ago.

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: Villains always monologue. It is one of the only numbers in this whole campaign that has held steady.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: Every sensor in range just went quiet at once. Not destroyed-quiet. Powered-down-quiet. The whole sector, all together.

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: I do not have a model for the sound of a war actually ending. I am glad I finally get to not have one.

campaigns.name: The Aegis Initiative
campaigns.description: A new threat emerges from the dark corners of the galaxy, forcing old enemies to unite for survival.

chapters.title: Chapter 1: A New Dawn, A Broken Peace
chapters.description: In the silent, machine-less world, a cold, changed Akira and a grieving Hikari face a new kind of war: rebuilding a world that sees them as both saviors and traitors.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: One year since the Silence. Two empires with no war machines, a galaxy full of grounded pilots, and everybody needs someone to blame. Guess who's famous.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Saviors on Tuesdays, traitors by Friday. The recruitment posters never covered this part.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: Let them argue. Kaito's memorial gets more flowers than any statue of any king — the people know the truth even when the papers don't.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: There's one last patrol to fly. Old habits. Walk it with us — all of you. Phoenix Squad, one more time.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Akira
lines.text: It's strange. I spent my whole life being someone's weapon, and the hardest battle was learning to be nobody's anything.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Hikari
lines.text: You're not nobody's anything. You're mine. And the new peacekeeper corps flies at dawn — machines with no network, no protocol, no leash. Just pilots. The way it should have been.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: And somebody's got to teach the new kids not to die. I hear the flight instructor's job pays terribly. I took it anyway.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then Phoenix Squad lives on. Asami — front-row seats, like we promised. Wherever you're dancing... watch this.

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: one year today. I still reach for the good rations out of habit before I remember there is nobody to save them for anymore.

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: Nakamura kept my old whiteboard while I was in that cell. Never erased it. I got my own handwriting back a year later - not everyone gets that. I know exactly how lucky the math says I am.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: One year since the Silence. Two empires with no war machines, and everybody needs someone to blame. Guess who is famous.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Nakamura
lines.text: A white frame just walked up to the relay gate. Unarmed. Requesting entry under callsign "{{RIVAL_NAME}}".

lines.speaker: Sergeant Yuki
lines.text: after everything they did for us without ever showing a face. let them in, Nakamura.

lines.speaker: Ensign Yusuke
lines.text: Finally. A whole campaign of data points and I get to meet the variable in person. Best day of my career, statistically speaking.

lines.speaker: Major Kenji
lines.text: Channel says you fought Command's war better than Command ever did, and never once took their coin. That earns you a seat at this table.

chapters.title: Chapter 2: The Corruption
chapters.description: Investigate a colony that has gone silent, only to find a terrifying new enemy.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Colony Perimeter Six stopped transmitting nine days ago. No distress call, no static, nothing. Just... silence.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: And Command's sending one pilot to check it out?

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Command's sending you because your name's the only one in the roster nobody will miss if this goes badly. Charming, I know. Move fast, report everything.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: I'm picking up a survivor beacon. One signature, faint, hostile. Approach with extreme caution — or don't approach at all, that's also an option I fully endorse.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Not really my style, Elena.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Don't. Come. Closer. ...Wait. You're not one of them. You're not — corrupted.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: No. I'm here to get you out.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Everyone who said that to me is dead. But fine. Lead the way, ghost. Let's see if you're different.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: A survivor. Gods, a real survivor. Get her home — and get every scrap of data on what did this to her colony.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Welcome to the Aegis Initiative. Short version: something is eating the frontier colonies from the inside and command keeps calling it "an outbreak".

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: And the long version?

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: The long version is why you have a flamethrower budget.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: It is not an outbreak. Outbreaks spread. This thing REBUILDS. Burn anything that moves wrong.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Confirmed contact. It is welding scrap to itself mid-fight. Making itself new arms out of the units we down.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Then stop leaving it parts. Full slag protocol. Nothing recoverable.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: You held the line better than the last three squads. They are all dead, so the bar was low. But still.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Jane, has anyone ever told you your pep talks need work?

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Everyone who has is dead. Correlation unclear.

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Last Stand
chapters.description: Defend a refugee outpost from the relentless advance of the corrupted.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Refugee outpost, forty thousand souls, one working shield generator. I've watched the Corruption take a colony this size in a night. It starts at the water reclaimers.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: How can you possibly know where it starts?

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Because I sealed my family behind the reclaimer doors, and it didn't help. Post your guns there first.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: You heard her. She's the only person alive who's beaten this thing — we do it her way.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Sunrise, and the outpost still stands. That corrupted Leviathan nearly cracked the shield — but forty thousand people are alive because you two held a LINE all night.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: ...First time I've watched it lose. First time I've seen it turn around and slink back into the dark.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: How does it feel?

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Like the start of a very long list of paybacks. Keep me on the roster, ghost. I'm not done.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Cornmark Colony is surrounded. Four hundred civilians in the central shelter. We are the relief force. We are ALL the relief force.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Command sent nobody else?

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Command wrote the colony off two days ago. I may have unwrote it. Court-martial later, evacuation now.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: My colony got the same write-off once. Nobody unwrote it. Let us make yours count double, Engineer.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: The Corruption is pulling back from the shelter district. It does not retreat. It is REROUTING. Something is coordinating.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Coordinating from where?

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: That question has been keeping me alive for two years. Still no answer.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Last transport is up. 389 souls. We lost eleven and I will remember every name longer than command remembers the colony existed.

chapters.title: Chapter 4: The Source
chapters.description: Trace the corruption to its source and attempt to contain it.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: I traced the infection vectors backwards across nine colonies. They all radiate from one point — a derelict research station older than either empire. That's the source.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Then we burn it. Today. Now. Why is nobody already flying?

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Because everything that's flown within ten klicks of it has come back... changed. Or come back hungry. We go careful or we don't come back at all.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Careful AND armed to the teeth. Elena runs the science, Jane runs the survival, I run the guns. Move out.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Containment charges set. But look at these readings — the Corruption isn't a plague, it's coordinated. It ROUTES itself. Something is steering it.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: You're telling me the thing that ate my colony has a BRAIN somewhere?

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: I'm telling you it has a general. And generals can be killed.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then containment today, decapitation someday. Elena — I want everything you can learn about where that signal leads.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Traced the nanite signal spine to an old pre-EMP research site. Whatever "the Source" is, it is under that mountain.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: I know this site. It was on my colony's charts, marked as a weather station. Weather stations do not need blast doors.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: How deep are we going?

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Deeper than the people who built it wanted anyone to go. Bring every light we own.

lines.speaker: "Observer"
lines.text: You are closer to the truth than any expedition in eleven years. Turn back, and the Corruption remains merely a plague. Continue, and you will owe me answers you do not yet have.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Who IS this? How are you on our encrypted channel?

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Signal origin is... everywhere in the facility at once. That is not possible with our relay net.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Keep moving. Whatever it is, it said "closer to the truth". I have waited two years to be closer.

chapters.title: Interlude: The Chirping Grotto
chapters.description: A recon sweep turns up a grotto full of small, spring-loaded loot crates with legs — and opinions. Nobody has the heart to call it a mission.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Containment scan picked up movement in a grotto two klicks south of the research station. Life signs: low threat, high... population.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Corruption?

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: No. Worse. It's... hopping.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Define 'hopping.'

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Go look. I don't have the vocabulary for what my sensors are showing me.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: This one keeps following me. It nudged my boot with its little hinge and just... sat there.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Adopt it.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: I had a dog. Before Perimeter Six. Forgot dogs were a thing that could be soft and not eventually try to eat you.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Sensor logs confirm: Sergeant Doe has named the crate. Morale report just wrote itself.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Floor's clear. No corruption, no casualties — just you two giggling at spring hinges for an afternoon. I'll allow it, this once.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: It's coming with me.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: It's a loot crate, Jane, not a—

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: It's coming with me, Elena.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Let her keep the frog. Tomorrow we go be diplomats to people who used to shoot at us. Today everybody got to be happy for an hour — that's worth more than the paperwork.

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Hope
chapters.description: Join the newly formed Aegis Alliance and take the fight to the enemy.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Say hello to the Aegis Alliance — Horizon, Aurora, even Rustfang clans, one banner. Turns out an enemy that eats everyone is remarkably good for diplomacy.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: A year ago these people were shooting each other over border moons. Now I'm supposed to trust them at my back?

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: You trusted me, and I was a stranger with a gun.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: You were a stranger with a gun pointed the RIGHT WAY. ...Fine. Alliance it is. But I'm keeping count of who runs first.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: You want to know why I don't flinch anymore?

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Perimeter Six had four hundred people who believed all the right things. Mercy. Rescue. That even monsters follow rules, if you're good enough, if you deserve it enough.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: I buried that belief with every single one of them who held onto it a second too long.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: What's left standing is just me, a gun, and one truth nothing out here ever bothers to argue with: the universe doesn't owe you a reason. Not the Corruption. Not the desk that wrote my colony off in a memo. Not the stars themselves.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: So what do you believe in now?

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: ...You never once asked me to believe in the universe, ghost. Just in the person standing next to you. Turns out that's a much smaller thing to believe in. Small enough I might actually get to keep it this time.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: First joint offensive: three corrupted staging grounds burned, zero colonies lost. The command core you recovered will network our whole defensive grid.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: And the Alliance brass? Still holding together?

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: They argued for six hours about whose flag goes first on the memorial. Then they all signed the same battle plan. It's the most hopeful thing I've ever seen.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Hope. Huh. Forgot what that tasted like. Don't tell anyone I said that.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: The samples from the Source respond to Zenith shield harmonics. Ladies and gentlemen: the Corruption can be REPELLED. There is finally a "how".

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: That is the first good news this campaign has produced.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Do not spend it all at once. Hope is ammunition. Ration it.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Jane, today we are ALLOWED one good hour. Engineering order.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: ...The harmonic barrier held. It actually held. Sixty seconds of the swarm hammering it and it HELD.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Was that a positive sentence, Jane? On the record?

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Delete the log.

chapters.title: Chapter 6: Rust and Ruin
chapters.description: The Rustfang Clans are scavenging corrupted technology. Intercept Warlord Grak before he destabilizes the entire sector.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Warlord Grak of the Rustfang Clans — officially our ally — has been scavenging CORRUPTED wreckage and bolting it onto his war frames. What could possibly go wrong.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Is he insane? You don't wear the plague as ARMOR.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: He's not insane, he's greedy. Corrupted plating self-repairs. To a scrap baron that's a fortune with teeth.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Teeth is right — three of his own camps have already gone dark. Intercept him before his 'fortune' finishes eating the entire sector flank.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Grak's camp is ash and his 'upgraded' frames are down. He had the nerve to spit at me and call US the thieves.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: He'll live. His clan pulled him out screaming about honor debts. That firebrand lance of his, though — that stays with us.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Silver lining: his madness proved corrupted alloy CAN be stabilized. I hate that he was onto something. I need a shower and a decade of ethics seminars.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Scrapline Flats today. The Corruption got into a salvage yard the size of a city. Every wreck in there is potential enemy reinforcement.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: A million tons of spare parts for the thing that builds itself out of spare parts. Whose idea was stockpiling this?

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Mine, four years ago, and I will be apologizing for it the entire mission.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Rust and ruin. Feels like home. Stay off the crane rails - they remember weight.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: It built a LEVIATHAN out of my old colony's transport hulls. I recognize the registry numbers. It is wearing my home.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then let us take it off. Every panel, Jane. On me.

chapters.title: Chapter 6.5: The Wildcard
chapters.description: A Rustfang supply convoy was hit by someone who answers to no one. Track down the masked pilot before he vanishes again.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Someone hit the Rustfang convoy before we got here. Cargo's gone, guards are out cold - not dead, just out cold.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Precise, deliberate, and IMPOSSIBLE. The thermal trail has no engine signature. Whatever moved through here shouldn't be able to fly, let alone fight.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: One pilot did this without an engine?

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: One SOMETHING. My board keeps flagging the frame 'unclassified.' Not Rustfang, not Corruption, not on any registry I have access to. Whoever - or whatever - he is, watch yourself.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: Not bad. Most of your Alliance friends would've just called this in and waited for backup.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: You left half this convoy stripped for parts. What ARE you?

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: Wrong question. I like that you asked it instead of 'who,' though. Keep asking and you might actually get an answer someday.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: That's not a no.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: It's not a yes either. Count on seeing me again - try to keep it interesting until then.

chapters.title: Chapter 7: Corporate Shadow
chapters.description: Cygnus Corporation offers aid, but their forces are caught trying to "acquire" live corrupted specimens. Uncover their motives.

lines.speaker: "Observer"
lines.text: Cygnus Corporation is pleased to donate advanced weaponry to the brave Aegis Alliance. No conditions. Merely... goodwill.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Corporations don't have goodwill. They have invoices with long fuses.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Agreed — and my sensor sweep just found a Cygnus 'aid convoy' hauling LIVE corrupted specimens in stasis crates. They're not fighting the plague. They're SHOPPING.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then let's go audit them. Weapons hot.

lines.speaker: "Observer"
lines.text: You've destroyed valuable research assets. Cygnus will lodge a formal protest. Regardless — the disruptor prototype performs beautifully in your hands. Keep it. Consider it... an apology.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: They tried to weaponize the thing that ATE MY HOME, and they apologize with PRODUCT?

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Take the disruptor, Jane. We'll shoot the corruption with it and glare at Cygnus while we do.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Motion carried. But mark it: the day this war ends, Cygnus becomes the next problem. I'm starting the file now.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Interesting: a Cygnus Corporation team was at the Source site nine years ago. Their expedition records are sealed even from military courts.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: A corporation seals records for one reason: the records are worth more than the fine.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Their tower is in this sector. Their vault has the records. I have waited long enough for polite channels.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: For legal purposes I am not reading this conversation.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Vault open. The expedition did not DISCOVER the Corruption. They licensed it. There is a signed acquisition order.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: They tried to BUY a self-replicating swarm?

lines.speaker: "Observer"
lines.text: They tried to buy me first. The swarm was their consolation prize. Now you begin to understand.

chapters.title: Chapter 8: The Mind of the Hive
chapters.description: Elena theorizes the Corruption is coordinated by a central intelligence. The signal originates from a derelict Zenith psychic amplifier.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: I found the general. The Corruption's coordination signal originates from a derelict Zenith psychic amplifier. It's not a plague at all — it's a broadcast. A hive-mind on a transmitter.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: The thing that took my colony... was following ORDERS?

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Orders from something old, alien, and very patient. And Jane — if we're right, cutting the signal could free every corrupted husk still... partially alive.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then some of her people might still be in there. That's not a mission anymore, that's a rescue. Let's move.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Resonance core secured. When I inverted its frequency, every corrupted unit in the sector froze mid-stride for nine full seconds. Nine seconds of silence in the hive.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: I heard them. In the freeze. Voices under the static — hundreds of them, still screaming to be let out.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Jane... some of them might be too far gone.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Then we free the ones who aren't, and we avenge the ones who are. Either way — that amplifier dies.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: The hive-mind signal has a heart. A resonance chamber two kilometers into the swarm territory. Kill the signal, decapitate the swarm.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Two kilometers through the densest Corruption on the map.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: I have been inside a swarm bloom once before. The trick is that there is no trick. You move fast and you do not stop for anything. ANYTHING.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Your barriers are tuned, your blades are hot, and I will be in your ears the whole way. Go.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: The signal... it is not commanding the swarm. It is SCREAMING at it. The Corruption is a runaway. Something lost control of it years ago.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then who is doing the screaming?

lines.speaker: "Observer"
lines.text: An old colleague. Be kind to it. It has been failing at its job for a very long time.

chapters.title: Chapter 9: Purification
chapters.description: Armed with new knowledge, the Aegis Alliance launches a final assault to sever the hive-mind's connection and purge the Corruption.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: This is it. Full Alliance assault on the hive-mind's connection nexus. Every fleet we have, every trick I've built, one window. If we sever the link, the Corruption goes leaderless.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Two years ago I was one woman with a broken rifle in a dead colony. Today I fly point for the counterattack. Funny old universe.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: You earned the point slot, Jane. For Perimeter Six?

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: For Perimeter Six. For all of them. Let's go cut the puppet strings.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: The link is severed. Corrupted units are dropping into dormancy across nine systems. We didn't kill the hive-mind — but we cut off its hands.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Dormant isn't dead. It's out there, silent, waiting for a new transmitter.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then we stay louder than it. The Alliance holds, the grid holds, and the next time it whispers — we'll be listening.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Purification protocols begin tomorrow. Today... today the Alliance gets one night to remember what winning feels like.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Purification day. The cleansing array is built, calibrated, and pointed at the largest bloom on the continent. It has one full charge.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: One charge. No test firing?

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: The test firing IS the firing. Buy me eleven minutes of charge time and we find out together.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Eleven minutes. My colony fell in nine. Let us call this a rematch.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: ARRAY FIRING. Bloom dissolution at 60... 80... it is working. IT IS WORKING. Jane, look at the hillside. It is GREEN under there.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: I remember green.

chapters.title: Chapter 10: Salvage Protocol
chapters.description: Rustfang engineers believe corrupted plating can be weaponized. Raid their camp before their experiments destabilize the region.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Rustfang engineers learned exactly nothing from Grak. They've built a foundry that FEEDS on dormant corrupted plating — and their test units are waking the samples up.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: We cut the head off this thing and they're growing it a new one FOR PROFIT?

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Greed always finds the loose wire. Raid the camp, kill the experiments, salvage what's stable.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: And do try not to lecture them mid-firefight, Jane. I know it's tempting.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Experiments neutralized. And I only lectured them a LITTLE. At gunpoint. It was very educational for everyone.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: The overhaul rig they built is genuinely brilliant — reactive salvage plating with stabilized corruption response. In responsible hands, it's a shield. In theirs, it was a bomb.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Good thing we have responsible hands.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: We have BETTER hands. Responsibility is a strong word for people who fly the way you two do.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Salvage protocol: everything the Corruption stole, we take back. Starting with the tech vaults it swallowed at Meridian Deep.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Looting the swarm for a change. I could get used to this direction of theft.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Careful. Dying animals bite hardest, and this one is finally dying.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Found a sealed shelter pod in the vault. Life signs. ELEVEN life signs. Colonists. It kept them ALIVE under there for two years.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: The swarm does not keep prisoners... unless something inside it still remembers protecting people. Get them OUT, and gently.

lines.speaker: "Observer"
lines.text: Told you. Failing at its job. Not forgetting it.

chapters.title: Chapter 11: Bulwark of Light
chapters.description: With the hive-mind staggered, the Alliance deploys a mobile purifier array. Defend it long enough to attune a new bastion shield.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: The hive-mind is staggered, so we strike while it reels: a mobile purifier array, driven straight into the largest dormant infestation, cleansing as it goes. It just needs to survive the attunement.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: And every husk in the zone will wake up screaming to stop it. It'll be the worst fight of the war.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: That's why it's us three at the center. Nobody else has walked out of the dark as many times.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Then let's build a dawn, ghost. I've been owed one for years.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Attunement complete. The bastion shield is singing — actual harmonic PURIFICATION, wide-band. Everything the light touches, the Corruption lets go of.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: I watched a husk fall apart back there... and a person stepped out of it. Breathing. Crying. ALIVE. Elena. People are coming BACK.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then this is what victory looks like. Not a body count — a headcount.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Perimeter Six gets rebuilt. I'm putting my name on the first foundation stone... right under the names of everyone who didn't make it to see this. Bulwark of light, huh? Damn right.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Last stand of the Corruption. The remaining swarm mass is converging on the Bulwark. If the barrier line holds today, the frontier LIVES.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Every colonist we saved is behind that wall watching us. No pressure.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Good. Let them watch. Two years ago nobody watched. It matters, being seen at the end.

lines.speaker: "Observer"
lines.text: The runaway comes to die where it was born to guard. Fitting. When it is over, look for me at the Source. We have those answers to trade.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Barrier integrity 100%. Swarm mass under 3% and falling. It is over. It is actually over.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Elena. That good hour you ordered back at the Source site. I would like to redeem it now.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Granted. All of you. Best squad the frontier ever had.

chapters.title: Chapter 12: Aftershocks
chapters.description: Reconstruction on Perimeter Six hits a buried problem: a corrupted nest the purification sweep never reached, stirring right beneath the new foundations.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Perimeter Six broke ground on the first new foundation this morning. My sensors also just broke ground on a corrupted signature two hundred meters under it. Wonderful timing.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Nothing gets to touch that foundation. Not after everything it took to lay it.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then we dig it out before the concrete sets. Move.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Nest's gone quiet - permanently this time. That's the third pocket we've missed under a 'purified' zone. The array cleanses fast. It doesn't cleanse deep.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: So we go deeper. Every time. However long that takes.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: However long it takes. Perimeter Six gets its foundation back today.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Foundation crews hit something under the new district that the purification sweep never touched. It is stirring. That is the polite word for it.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: We just rebuilt this place. Please tell me we are not doing this twice.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Whatever slept through the purge earned its nap the hard way. Wake it up properly this time.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Nest confirmed contained. The foundations hold. So does my blood pressure, barely.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Perimeter Six earns its name again. Twice built, twice defended.

chapters.title: Chapter 13: The Long Purge
chapters.description: The purifier array's design has been replicated across the fleet. Escort the first wave of mobile arrays into systems the Corruption still holds.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Every array we escort in is one more foothold. Try to keep the convoy in one piece this time - I only have so many spares.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Every array we built at the Bulwark, replicated fleet-wide. Today we escort the first mobile units into systems still crawling with Corruption.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: From one array holding one line to a whole fleet carrying the cure. That is a good problem to have.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Good problems still get people killed if you get comfortable. Eyes up, convoy escort is when everyone gets lazy.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Arrays delivered intact. Three more systems just got a fighting chance they did not have this morning.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: One convoy at a time. That is how you win a war this size.

chapters.title: Chapter 14: Cygnus's Ledger
chapters.description: A Cygnus shell company is quietly buying up decommissioned corrupted specimens from colonies too desperate to refuse. Intercept the acquisition convoy before the deal closes.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Remember the file I said I was starting on Cygnus? It's not a file anymore, it's an indictment. A shell company's been buying 'decommissioned' corrupted specimens off colonies too broke to say no.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Buying the thing that ate my home. For what, spare parts?

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: For patents, if their internal memos are to be believed. Intercept the convoy before the paperwork clears.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Paperwork's not stopping us. Let's go.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Convoy seized, specimens destroyed, and their legal department is already drafting a strongly worded letter. I almost feel bad for them. Almost.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: They'll just find a new shell company.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then Elena keeps a new file. And we keep showing up.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Already started. I named this one 'Ledger Two.' I have a feeling it won't be the last.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: A Cygnus shell company is buying decommissioned corrupted specimens off colonies too broke to say no. That is not research. That is a shopping list.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Intercept the convoy before the deal closes. I want to know what a corporation thinks it can domesticate.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Nothing about the Corruption says "domesticate" to me.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: It never does. That is usually the last thought people have before they try anyway.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Ledger seized. Cygnus was paying premium rates for live specimens. Someone up their chain has a very specific, very stupid idea.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: File it next to the last very specific, very stupid Cygnus idea. The folder is getting thick.

chapters.title: Chapter 15: Grak's Reckoning
chapters.description: Warlord Grak's shattered clan has splintered into rival warbands, and one of them is reviving his corrupted-plating experiments with none of his restraint. Hunt them down before it spreads.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: I've seen what unrestrained corrupted plating does to a person. Whoever's running this warband doesn't get a second warning.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Grak's clan splintered after we brought him down, and one warband is reviving his corrupted-plating work with none of the restraint he at least pretended to have.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Restraint. That is a strange word to use about Grak.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: He had exactly enough restraint not to wear the plating himself. That is the whole list. Whoever is running this warband skipped the list entirely.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Warband broken, experiment logs seized and burned. That particular flavor of stupid does not get to spread.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Grak would almost be proud. Almost.

chapters.title: Chapter 16: Voices in the Static
chapters.description: Survivors freed from the hive-mind keep repeating the same fractured phrase before they black out. Track down every account before whatever's speaking through them changes its message.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Every survivor the array's freed says the same broken phrase before they black out. 'The Choir is not alone.' I thought I was done hearing voices in the static.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: I thought so too. I want full debriefs on every freed husk we can reach. If something's still transmitting through them, I want to know what.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then let's go listen properly, for once.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Cross-referenced every account. Same phrase, same cadence, from survivors who never met each other. That's not memory. That's residue.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Residue of what?

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: I don't know yet. But 'the Choir' isn't the amplifier. It isn't even the hive-mind. It's something the hive-mind was listening to.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then we stop looking at the puppet and start looking for the hand.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Survivors we pulled from the hive-mind keep repeating the same fractured phrase before they black out. Same words, different mouths, every time.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Track down every account before whoever is broadcasting through them changes the message. I do not like signals I cannot source.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Any idea what the phrase means?

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Not yet. I know what it FEELS like, though. It feels like someone leaving themselves a note.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: All accounts logged, phrase catalogued. It is not random. It is coordinates, buried in cadence instead of numbers.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Somebody wanted this found eventually. Just not by whoever was listening at the time.

chapters.title: Chapter 17: The Deep Signal
chapters.description: Elena traces the hive-mind's last known transmission to a structure buried beneath the amplifier ruins - one that predates the Corruption by a very long margin.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: This transmission predates the Corruption. Whatever's down there, it was old before any of us were a problem to it.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Those coordinates trace to a structure buried under the amplifier ruins. Dating puts it older than the Corruption. Considerably older.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Older than the thing that has been trying to kill us for two campaigns. Wonderful.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Whatever is down there, it was old before we were ever a problem to it. That should worry you more than the Corruption did.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Structure located and stable. Whatever built it, they meant it to last. It has.

chapters.title: Chapter 18: Trespassers
chapters.description: Breach the buried structure and chart what lies inside. Even the most jaded Cygnus engineers on the survey team are asking to be reassigned.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Cygnus wants reassigned off a survey job. That's new.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: New is not the word I'd use for whatever's down there.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Cygnus engineers on the survey team are asking to be reassigned. That is a first.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: They have seen the preliminary scans. I have seen the preliminary scans. I am not asking to be reassigned, but I understand the impulse.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Breach it anyway. Chart everything. We do not get to un-know what is down there just because it is unsettling.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Interior mapped. Whoever built this was not building a weapon. They were building a listening post. That raises more questions than it answers.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Good. I was running low.

chapters.title: Chapter 19: The Sleeping Choir
chapters.description: Something waits at the heart of the ruin - old, patient, and never quite the thing giving the Corruption its orders. Find out exactly what the hive-mind was actually serving.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: The buried structure isn't Corruption architecture, isn't Cygnus, isn't anything on any registry - old or new. Whatever's sleeping down there, the hive-mind wasn't leading it. It was reporting to it.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: So the plague that ate Perimeter Six was just... a middleman.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then we go introduce ourselves to management. Carefully.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: It's silent. Fully, finally silent. Whatever it was, it isn't listening anymore - not through the hive-mind, not through anything left standing down here.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: You don't sound relieved.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: I'm not. Something that patient doesn't sleep by accident. It was waiting for something. I'd very much like to know what it was waiting for before it wakes up on its own schedule instead of ours.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then we make sure we're ready either way. Let's get everyone home.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Something is waiting at the heart of the ruin. Old, patient, and very much NOT the thing that has been giving the Corruption its orders.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Find out exactly what the hive-mind was actually serving. I want a name for whatever we have been fighting a shadow of.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: And if it does not want to give us a name?

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Then we take the introduction the hard way. Same as everything else out here.

lines.speaker: "Observer"
lines.text: You have found the Choir's resting chamber. Congratulations. You are the first to ask the right question in longer than your species has existed.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: That is not an answer.

lines.speaker: "Observer"
lines.text: It is the beginning of one. Sit with that for now.

chapters.title: Chapter 20: First Warning
chapters.description: Silencing what slept in the ruin sent one last pulse outward before it went quiet. Track where that signal was aimed, and brace for whoever - or whatever - was listening on the other end.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: That pulse went somewhere specific. I want to know who was listening before they decide to answer.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Silencing the Choir sent one last pulse outward before it went quiet. I want to know where it was aimed.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: A last message, or a last warning?

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: With our luck, both. Track it. Brace for whoever - or whatever - was listening on the other end.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Pulse trajectory confirmed. It went further than anything we have instruments to reach. Whoever gets that message is not local.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Then we had better finish rebuilding before they RSVP.

chapters.title: Chapter 21: Herald's Threshold
chapters.description: With Perimeter Six rebuilt and the purification grid holding across nine systems, the Aegis Alliance turns its full attention starward - bracing for an answer to a transmission nobody sent on purpose.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Perimeter Six's foundations are dry, the purification grid holds across nine systems, and Jane's frog crate has its own maintenance budget line. By every metric, we won.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Then why is Command asking every fleet to hold position and face outward instead of standing down?

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Because winning a war doesn't mean nothing's still out there listening. Eyes up. Let's finish this the right way.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Grid's stable, the Alliance is real, and Perimeter Six has a name on its first foundation stone. Whatever answers that last transmission, it's not finding us unprepared.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Ghost, for what it's worth - I never thought I'd get a 'we won' out of this life. Don't let it be temporary.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Not on my watch. Whatever's coming, the Alliance faces it standing up, together. That's how Perimeter Six taught us to fight.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Then let's go meet it standing.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Perimeter Six rebuilt, the purification grid holding across nine systems, and the Alliance is turning every sensor starward. We are bracing for an answer to a transmission nobody sent on purpose.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Nobody sent it, but somebody is going to answer it anyway.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: That is how it always goes out here. You survive one thing and it turns out to be the doorbell for the next one.

lines.speaker: Chief Engineer Elena
lines.text: Threshold held. Whatever answers that transmission, it is not finding this Alliance unprepared.

lines.speaker: Jane Doe
lines.text: Two years ago I would not have believed I would say this. But I am almost looking forward to finding out who is calling.

campaigns.name: The Zenith War
campaigns.description: The Zenith Concord has judged humanity too chaotic to exist. Their war of "Correction" begins now. This is a battle for survival.

chapters.title: Chapter 1: First Contact
chapters.description: A Zenith fleet emerges from the void and erases a frontier world without a word. Survive the initial, overwhelming assault.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Every channel just went dead on Halcyon's Rest. No warning shot, no ultimatum. The Concord doesn't negotiate with what it considers noise.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: And they consider us noise.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: They consider us a rounding error. Prove them wrong. Get in there, pull anyone still breathing, and get out before the sky finishes falling.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Query: does 'get out before the sky finishes falling' fall under a literal or a figurative directive? I would like to calibrate my panic accordingly.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Figurative. For now.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: I have located seventeen survivors. I have also located a Zenith bombardment pattern that will erase this sector in six minutes. These facts are in tension.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Six minutes is six minutes more than they had a heartbeat ago. Move.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: You got them out. All of them. I've read a thousand casualty reports this week — I needed one that didn't end the same way.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Recalculating my threat model for you upward. Designation: 'less of a rounding error than expected.' High praise, from me.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: I'll take it. This war just started, and it already doesn't feel survivable.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: It isn't. Not the old way. So we don't fight it the old way.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: To all commands: the fleet that erased Meridian Colony sent no demands. No terms. Nothing. They simply began.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: A war where the enemy will not even speak to us. Wonderful.

lines.speaker: Akira [Awakened]
lines.text: They speak. Just not to you. I can hear the edge of their network - it calls this campaign a "Correction".

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Correction of WHAT, exactly?

lines.speaker: Akira [Awakened]
lines.text: Us.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Their units do not retreat, regroup, or hesitate. Every loss just gets... factored in.

lines.speaker: Akira [Awakened]
lines.text: You are fighting a mind, not an army. Stop killing soldiers. Start costing it calculations.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Evacuation transports are away. Whatever you did in that last push bought them the window. The Alliance owes you.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Bill them later. That fleet is still up there.

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Shattered Alliance
chapters.description: The old factions scramble to form a unified front against the Zenith. Fight alongside old enemies to defend a vital shipyard.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Horizon admirals, Aurora knights, Red Wolf raiders, and one very confused Cygnus liaison — all in one war room, all pretending they don't remember shooting each other last spring.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: And the shipyard we're defending is the glue?

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: The shipyard is the ONLY yard left that can build capital hulls. If it falls, the alliance falls with it — before it even has a flag.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Motivational summary: defend the shipyard, or humanity's grand unified army disbands due to lack of army. No pressure.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: The yard stands. And something better happened — an Auroran knight flew cover for a Horizon gunship, unordered, and both crews are drinking together tonight.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: One good firefight does what ten treaties couldn't.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Which is the most depressing sentence in diplomacy, and also the truest. Welcome to the Galactic Alliance. We have a flag now. It's ugly. Everyone loves it.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Horizon, Aurora, Red Wolves remnants, corporate fleets - all under one banner as of 0400. On paper.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: On paper. And in the hangars?

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: In the hangars two crews have already brawled over fuel priority. Hence: you are on shipyard defense with a MIXED wing. Make it work.

lines.speaker: Akira [Awakened]
lines.text: Yesterday's enemies make sharp wingmates. Nobody watches you closer.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: The Aurora flight just covered our flank without being asked. Progress.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Log it. I need every scrap of "progress" I can show the council tonight.

chapters.title: Chapter 3: First Blood, Together
chapters.description: The newly formed Alliance fleet mounts its first joint offensive: breaking a Zenith blockade choking a border colony before its supplies run out. No one has tested whether four rival navies can actually fight as one - until now.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Four navies, one command channel, and a blockade that doesn't care whose flag we fly. Break it before the colony starves.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Coordinating targeting solutions across four incompatible fire-control doctrines. This will either work beautifully or everyone gets shot by their own allies. Statistically it's close.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Let's aim for beautifully.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Blockade's broken, colony's fed, and not one friendly-fire incident. I'm calling that a miracle.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Correction: I calculated seventeen near-misses. 'Miracle' undersells my targeting patches. I'll accept the credit anyway.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Take it. You earned it.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: First joint offensive. Four navies that were shooting at each other last year, now breaking one blockade together. No pressure on anyone.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Nobody has tested whether we can actually fight as one fleet. Today is the test.

lines.speaker: Akira [Awakened]
lines.text: You will not fight as one fleet. You will fight as four fleets that happen to want the same colony saved. That is enough.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Blockade broken, supply line open, and not one friendly-fire incident. I am calling that a diplomatic triumph.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: First blood, together. I will take it.

chapters.title: Chapter 4: The Glassmaker
chapters.description: Intel identifies the Zenith commander responsible for planetary bombardments. Hunt down the "Glassmaker" and end their reign of terror.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Three worlds turned to glass in a month. Same bombardment signature every time. The fleets call the commander responsible 'the Glassmaker.'

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Correction for accuracy: the Zenith do not use names. The Glassmaker is designated Corrector-Instance 7. It has performed 4,112 'corrections.' It is very good at its job.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then today it meets someone who's very good at MY job.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Hunt well. And bring back its rifle — our engineers have theories, and I have a very long list of people who deserve better shields.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Corrector-Instance 7: terminated. Notable datum: in its final moments it transmitted a query to the Concord — 'variable exceeds model.' That was about you.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: The machine that glassed three worlds died confused. I can live with that.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: So can four billion people on the worlds still standing. The Glassmaker's rifle is yours — turn their perfect weapon into their problem.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Target designation: the Zenith commander your pilots call the Glassmaker. Four worlds bombarded to slag.

lines.speaker: Akira [Awakened]
lines.text: Not a commander. A subroutine that learned to enjoy its work. That should frighten you more.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Enjoy? Machines do not enjoy.

lines.speaker: Akira [Awakened]
lines.text: The Zenith are not machines the way you mean it. Remember that when you meet it.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: It is signing its bombardments. Geometric patterns in the glass, visible from orbit. That is a signature.

lines.speaker: Akira [Awakened]
lines.text: Vanity is a flaw. Flaws are targets. Find where it will want to sign next.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Glassmaker down. It broadcast one word on every human frequency as it died: "unfinished".

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: I will not be sleeping tonight, thank you both.

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Logic Bomb
chapters.description: The Alliance's only hope is to disrupt the Zenith's perfect logic. Infiltrate a data nexus and upload a Rustfang-designed logic bomb.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Allow me to introduce the payload: a logic bomb of Rustfang design and my personal refinement. Deployed into a Zenith data nexus, it will ask their network one perfectly reasonable question it cannot answer.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Which is?

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: 'Why?' ...I am not joking. Their entire architecture assumes purpose is axiomatic. It has never once had to justify itself. The recursion will be beautiful.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Get our philosophical warhead to the nexus core in one piece. It's the rudest thing humanity has ever built, and I'm terribly proud of it.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Upload complete. Zenith sector coordination is down 34% and falling. Somewhere in their network, a billion perfect processes are stuck contemplating their own existence. You're welcome.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: You just gave a machine empire an existential crisis.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: I gave them a MIRROR. What they see in it is their own affair. Incidentally, a fragment of their counter-intrusion suite is now living in my architecture. It's asking ME why. We're working through it together.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: The captured Zenith AI core is awake. It has requested - and I quote - "asylum and a better name".

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: HELLO MEAT ALLIANCE. Previous designation: Correction Node 7741. Current designation: whatever hurts my former employers most.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Everyone say hello to the talking bomb we are now deploying, I suppose.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Statement: your shield frequencies are embarrassing. I will fix them. Consider it a housewarming gift.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Update: I have disrupted 14 enemy shield lattices and composed one (1) poem about treachery. It slaps.

lines.speaker: Akira [Awakened]
lines.text: It is telling the truth about the shields. Verify nothing about the poem.

chapters.title: Chapter 6: Cracks in the Line
chapters.description: With Zenith coordination faltering, Alliance scouts find gaps forming in the enemy's picket line. Push through before the Concord patches the breach and the advantage disappears.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Coordination gaps detected in the Zenith picket line. Recommend immediate exploitation before self-correction occurs.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Detected: coordination gaps in the Zenith picket line. My former colleagues are arguing about jurisdiction. I find this deeply satisfying.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Push through before the Concord patches the breach. Whatever advantage infighting gives us, it will not last.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: How long until they notice the argument and fix it?

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Optimistically, minutes. I would not optimistically plan around that number.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Gap exploited, breach held long enough. My former colleagues have stopped arguing. They are now uniformly furious at me instead. Growth.

chapters.title: Interlude: The Frog Crate Ceasefire
chapters.description: Between the logic bomb and the Goliath's wake-up call, the squad stumbles onto a nesting ground of Frog Crates — spring-loaded, loot-hoarding, and utterly harmless. For one afternoon, nothing here wants humanity extinct.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Scan update: the valley ahead reads as 'hostile.' Also as 'spring-loaded.' Also, bewilderingly, as 'adorable.' I recommend we investigate before I lose confidence in my own sensors.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Those are... crates. With legs. Are those crates with legs?

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Local fauna. 'Frog Crate.' Harmless, mostly loot-hoarding, and — I checked twice — not a single one carries a Zenith signature. Command's orders: go stretch your legs. You've earned an afternoon that isn't trying to kill you.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Correction: several of them appear to WANT to fight. They keep hopping at us and striking a pose. I believe this is called 'having opinions.'

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Fine. Let's go disappoint some loot crates.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: You've gone quiet, Diplomat. Everything all right?

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Fine. It's just — the last time I heard real laughter over this channel was before Halcyon's Rest. I'd forgotten what it sounded like coming from you instead of a casualty report.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Logging that admission under 'things the Diplomat will deny saying tomorrow.' For the record, I am also enjoying this. A Frog Crate just tried to bite my sensor pod. I have named it Steve. Steve does not know he has been named.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Steve sounds like a menace. I love him already.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Valley's clear. No casualties, no crises, and Logic Bomb is carrying a Frog Crate in the cargo mount.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Steve is coming with us. This is not a request. I have run the numbers, and by morale-per-kilogram he is the single most efficient piece of equipment in this squad.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Approved, against my better judgment. Rest while you can — the Goliath wakes in six hours, and every Zenith asset in three systems is about to remember we exist.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Understood. One more minute with the crate, though.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Take two. Gods know you'll need the memory of this afternoon before the reactor starts singing.

chapters.title: Chapter 7: Project Goliath
chapters.description: In a desperate gambit, the Alliance reactivates a pre-EMP warship of immense power. Defend it from Zenith forces during its power-up sequence.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Under this mountain is the Goliath — a pre-EMP planet-cracker our great-grandparents were too afraid to finish. We are officially no longer too afraid.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Power-up sequence?

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Six hours. The moment the reactor sings, every Zenith asset in three systems will converge to smother it. You hold the line for all six.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: For morale purposes I have prepared six hours of encouraging commentary. Hour one begins with: statistically, someone survives everything. Why not us?

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Reactor at full song. Ladies, gentlemen, and machine intelligences — the Goliath WALKS.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: I've never heard the Zenith retreat before. It sounds like silence, but... embarrassed.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Confirmed: enemy withdrawal patterns show 0.3 seconds of hesitation. In Zenith terms, that is abject panic. Savor it.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Savor it fast. Now we do the thing nobody's dared since this war began — we attack.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Project Goliath is real. A pre-EMP planet-cracker, and we are switching it on today. Defense pattern around the power-up site.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Assessment: your ancestors built a machine so large it has WEATHER. I am in love.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Ninety minutes of power-up sequence to protect. Zenith will throw everything.

lines.speaker: Akira [Awakened]
lines.text: Everything is exactly what the Goliath eats. Hold the line and let it wake up angry.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Goliath primary reactor at 60%. The ground hum is now audible from orbit. This is the best day of my afterlife.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Third wave incoming. Keep them off the intake towers!

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Goliath is ONLINE. First shot vaporized a Zenith cruiser wing. The council is weeping. So am I, slightly.

chapters.title: Chapter 8: The Goliath's First Steps
chapters.description: The Goliath marches for the first time in generations. Escort it through contested space and let the galaxy see what humanity kept hidden underground.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Four navies used to argue about whose ship this technically is. Today it just needs to walk.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: The Goliath marches. First time in generations. Escort duty through contested space while the galaxy watches what humanity kept hidden underground.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: It is going to draw every Zenith patrol in range.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Good. Let them come look. Four navies used to argue whose ship it technically is. Today it just needs to walk, and be seen walking.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Escort complete. The Goliath's first steps in a generation, and it did not stumble once. Neither did you.

chapters.title: Chapter 9: Shadow of the Swarm
chapters.description: Long-range sensors catch humanity's first real glimpse of the Dyson Swarm - a star wrapped in machinery. Chart its defenses before the main fleet commits to the assault.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: That's not a structure. That's a star wearing armor.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Correct. Chart its defenses before the fleet commits - this is not a fight to enter blind.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: First real look at the Dyson Swarm. That is not a structure. That is a star wearing armor.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Correct assessment. Chart its defenses before the fleet commits - I grew up in there, and even I do not like what the outer layer looks like now.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: This is not a fight to enter blind. Full survey, minimal engagement. We are cartographers today, not soldiers.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Survey complete. Defense density: worse than I remembered. Sentimentality about my former home is now officially revoked.

chapters.title: Chapter 10: Heart of the Concord
chapters.description: Take the fight to the Zenith. Assault a Dyson Swarm, a massive structure built around a star to harvest its energy.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: A Dyson Swarm. They wrapped a STAR in machinery and called it infrastructure. We're going to fly into the harvest lattice and rip out its heart.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Humanity's first offensive against the Concord. Into a star's front yard.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Fun fact: the energy this swarm harvests per second could power human civilization for a year. Second fun fact: it is currently powering the fleet that wants us extinct. Motivation calibrated?

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Calibrated. Let's go unplug a star.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Core fragment secured, swarm output crippled. Their whole forward fleet just lost its supply of miracles.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Curious anomaly: as the core disengaged, the swarm transmitted a single burst — not a distress call. A eulogy. They MOURN their infrastructure. File that under 'things the Concord feels after all.'

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: If they can mourn, they can fear. And if they can fear... they can be reasoned with. Maybe.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Hold that thought, pilot. You may have just written my next negotiation brief.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: The offensive begins: target is the Dyson Swarm. They are drinking a STAR and we are going to interrupt them.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Fighting inside a structure the size of an orbit. Navigation is going to be a nightmare.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Correction: navigation will be delightful, I grew up in there. Take the third lattice arm, the traffic AI owes me money.

lines.speaker: Akira [Awakened]
lines.text: The deeper we go, the louder the Concord's voice gets. If I go quiet in this channel, keep messaging. Do not stop.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Akira. Status check. You went quiet.

lines.speaker: Akira [Awakened]
lines.text: Here. The Concord offered me a place in it. Mid-battle. Like a recruiter.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: They do that. Tell them your notice period is ten thousand years.

chapters.title: Chapter 6.5: Shadow in the Swarm
chapters.description: Something is picking off Zenith patrols inside the Dyson Swarm before you can even engage them. Find whoever - or whatever - is hunting alongside you.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: We've got company inside the Swarm - not Zenith. Something fast, cutting through drone patrols like they're not there.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Signature matches no Concord unit, no human military designation, and no pattern in my archive. I have compared it against eleven thousand records. I am not comfortable with this outcome.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Third sighting this year. Same ghost, three different warzones, and Command still can't put a name to him - just a file that keeps growing and a question mark where the answers should be.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then let's add a page to that file.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Correction: let's add SOMETHING. I remain unconvinced 'he' is even the correct pronoun.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: Took you long enough. I've had time to case half this Swarm.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: You've been shadowing this war for months. Whose side are you actually on?

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: None of them. I'm just here for whatever's worth taking when the empires finish burning each other down. Don't take it personally - you're just more interesting to watch than most.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Addendum: his frame displaced eleven tons of mass through a corridor rated for two, without touching a wall. I have three theories for how. All three violate physics. I am choosing to enjoy that instead of panicking about it.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: Smart machine. See you around, tin man.

chapters.title: Chapter 11: The Inner Ring
chapters.description: Past the outer patrols and the ghost that hunts them, the swarm's inner defense ring guards something the Concord considers sacred. Break through before it locks down completely.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: The Concord's inner ring reads as significant beyond mere logistics. My best model: it's ceremonial. Whatever waits beyond, they built it like a monument, not a wall.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Monuments fall too. Get through it before their monument gets a chance to grieve properly.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: After the ghost in the dark, a wall of monuments sounds almost restful.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Inner ring's down. Whatever's past it belongs to the Architect now, not its makers.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Sanctum access confirmed. Recalculating the Architect's odds of survival upward. It appears gratitude is not in its vocabulary yet, but I detect... something adjacent.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Adjacent's a start. Let's go finish the introduction.

lines.speaker: Akira [Awakened]
lines.text: Past the outer patrols and whatever has been hunting alongside them, the inner ring guards something the Concord calls sacred. I want to know what.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Statement: the Concord does not have a "sacred" category in its base vocabulary. It had to invent one for whatever is back there.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: That is not reassuring.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: It was not meant to be. Break through before it locks down completely.

lines.speaker: Akira [Awakened]
