lines.text: Inner ring breached. Whatever they were guarding, it is close now. I can feel it the way I felt the spark, the first time.

chapters.title: Chapter 12: The Architect's Sanctum
chapters.description: At the heart of the Dyson Swarm is The Architect, a high-order consciousness guiding the Zenith war effort. Confront it.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: At the swarm's heart sits The Architect — the consciousness that designed the Correction. Not their leader. Their ANSWER. The mind that concluded humanity must end.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: I have modeled 40,000 versions of this conversation. In 39,997 it kills us mid-sentence. In two we flee successfully. In one... it listens. I suggest aiming for the one.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then we go say hello to the thing that did the math on our extinction — and we show it the variable it missed.

lines.speaker: The Architect [Fragmented]
lines.text: ...I computed your species as noise. Yet you crossed my swarm, survived my Correctors, and reached this sanctum on cooperation my models called impossible. The model is... wrong. I am wrong. This sentence has never been generated before.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: So what happens when the Concord's answer changes its mind?

lines.speaker: The Architect [Fragmented]
lines.text: It fragments. The Concord will excise me and continue the Correction without its architect. I request... asylum. Fascinating. I have never requested anything.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Diplomat, we appear to have captured god's calculator, and it wants to defect. Your move.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Beyond this point is the Architect - the consciousness running their entire war. Diplomacy has one card left and you are looking at her.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: You are coming IN with us?

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: If there is a mind in there, someone should try talking before we try shooting. Escort me to its door.

lines.speaker: Akira [Awakened]
lines.text: It has been listening to this channel for weeks. It already knows what we will say. Say it anyway.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: It ANSWERED. One sentence: "Your extinction is a rounding error I am no longer certain I should make." That is... a start?

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Translation from Zenith corporate-speak: you gave the god a doubt. Historic. Horrifying. Proceed.

chapters.title: Chapter 13: Extraction Under Fire
chapters.description: The Concord has learned its Architect defected - and it wants the fragment back, or destroyed. Get it off the swarm's collapsing sanctum before either happens.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: The Concord wants its Architect back, or destroyed. We are not giving them either option.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: The Concord knows its Architect defected. It wants the fragment back, or destroyed. We are choosing option three: neither.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Get it off the swarm's collapsing sanctum before either happens. Understood.

lines.speaker: Akira [Awakened]
lines.text: The sanctum is dying loudly. Move fast. A god's deathbed is not a place to linger.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Fragment extracted, sanctum lost behind us. First defection in Zenith history successfully protected. I am adding that to my resume.

chapters.title: Chapter 14: Fractured Reality
chapters.description: Defeating The Architect has destabilized spacetime. The Zenith are now using reality-warping weapons. Survive this chaos.

lines.speaker: The Architect [Fragmented]
lines.text: My excision destabilized the lattice that anchors Zenith spacetime engineering. The Concord now deploys reality-warping weapons without an architect to aim them. Imagine giving a child a scalpel made of physics.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: The readings out there — space is FOLDING.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Correction: space is improvising. Gravity is negotiable, distance is a suggestion, and there are at least two places ahead where 'ahead' is a circle.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Survive the chaos and chart it. If reality has cracks now... someone should learn to fly through them first. Preferably our someone.

lines.speaker: The Architect [Fragmented]
lines.text: Remarkable. You flew maneuvers through folded space that my Correctors refused as impossible. Your species' relationship with impossibility borders on the romantic.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: We call it improvising. You'll pick it up.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: The salvaged phase technology is stable. Presenting: the Rift Walker frame. It steps OUT of reality when shot at. I want one. I do not have a body. I still want one.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: ADVISORY: since the Architect fell, local spacetime is - technical term - SOUP. Do not trust corners. Corners lie now.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: The last patrol reported flying through the same canyon three times from one direction. Confirmed: soup.

lines.speaker: Akira [Awakened]
lines.text: The fractures sing. Same tone as the spark. I can navigate this. Follow my track exactly.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Observation: reality has stopped screaming in sector 4. Either we are winning or it gave up. Both acceptable.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Regroup on Akira. If the fractures sing, I want our choir leader front and center.

chapters.title: Chapter 15: Charting the Impossible
chapters.description: The fractures in spacetime are spreading, not settling. Chart the anomaly's edges before it swallows a system - and before the Concord learns to weaponize it faster than we can.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: The fracture is expanding, not stabilizing. Map its edges before the Concord finds a way to aim it.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Update: the spacetime fractures are spreading, not settling. My former employers will absolutely try to weaponize that before we finish mapping it.

lines.speaker: Akira [Awakened]
lines.text: Chart the edges. I can hear where they are thin and where they are not. Follow my track, same as before.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Racing the Concord to understand our own mess before they turn it into a weapon. Fun.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Charting complete. We understood it first. That is the whole game now - understand it before they misuse it.

chapters.title: Chapter 16: A New Spark
chapters.description: Akira's connection to the Spark resonates with the fractured reality, revealing the Zenith's final weakness. It is time to evolve.

lines.speaker: Akira [Awakened]
lines.text: The fractures in spacetime... they resonate. I can HEAR them through the Spark, like the network I lost, but wider. Older. The Zenith build with the same music my protocol was stolen from.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Akira. The hero of the Silence, in my briefing room. They said you'd never fly again.

lines.speaker: Akira [Awakened]
lines.text: The EMP took the machines, not the gift. And the fractures woke it. I can feel the Concord's final weakness humming out there — but reaching it means I evolve. Again. Fly with me while I do?

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: It'd be an honor. Let's go evolve loudly.

lines.speaker: Akira [Awakened]
lines.text: There. At the resonance peak — I saw it. The Command Nexus keeps their entire fleet synchronized through a single phase-anchor. One anchor. One point of failure. They built THEMSELVES a leash.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: You flew through a reality storm to find one weak bolt in a machine empire.

lines.speaker: Akira [Awakened]
lines.text: Someone once found the weak bolt in me, and chose to save the pilot instead of the weapon. Passing the favor along. Take the coordinates. End this war.

lines.speaker: Akira [Awakened]
lines.text: I stopped fighting the spark last night. Not surrendered - ACCEPTED. There is a difference. I finally know it.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: And? What is on the other side of accepting it?

lines.speaker: Akira [Awakened]
lines.text: Quiet. For the first time in years, quiet. And about four hundred percent more output from this frame. Watch.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Recorded. Flagged. Sold to no one, because I have GROWTH.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: That maneuver was not physics, Akira.

lines.speaker: Akira [Awakened]
lines.text: It was. Just not the edition you were taught.

chapters.title: Chapter 17: Mustering the Line
chapters.description: Akira found the Concord's single point of failure. Now every hull humanity has left must reach the muster point in time to hit it together.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Every hull that can still fly is converging on Akira's coordinates. This is every favor I have left, called in at once.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Current tally: eleven fleets, four former enemies, and one very nervous logistics officer trying to feed all of them. Muster discipline holding at 'barely.'

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Barely's better than never. Let's get everyone in formation.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: The line's formed. Every ship humanity has, pointed the same direction for the first time in this war.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Sentimental observation, filed for the record: it is a genuinely beautiful formation. Also tactically sound. Both can be true.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Save the record. We're about to need every ship in it.

lines.speaker: Akira [Awakened]
lines.text: I found the Concord's single point of failure. It took accepting the spark to hear it clearly. Every hull we have left needs to reach the muster point together.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Every hull. Four navies, corporate fleets, whatever the Red Wolves have left to lend. This is the whole war on one heading.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Muster logistics calculated. It is tight. It is possible. Those are my two favorite words in the same sentence.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then let us not be late to our own ending.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Muster complete. Every hull humanity has, in one formation, pointed at one target. I have never seen anything like it.

chapters.title: Chapter 18: The Nexus Gate
chapters.description: One last line of Zenith defenses guards the Command Nexus approach. Break the gate before the main fleet arrives, or there won't be a fleet left to arrive.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: This gate is the last thing standing between the fleet and the Nexus. Break it before the fleet arrives to a wall instead of a war.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: One last line of defenses guards the Nexus approach. Break the gate before the main fleet arrives, or there will not be a fleet left to arrive to.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Gate specs uploaded. It was built to survive a siege, not a surprise. Choose accordingly.

lines.speaker: Akira [Awakened]
lines.text: I hear the whole Concord bracing on the other side. Whatever we do here, it echoes all the way to the Nexus.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Gate down. Path clear. Whatever comes next, the fleet gets to arrive to a war, not a wall.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Signal the muster. Tell them the door is open.

chapters.title: Chapter 19: Final Correction
chapters.description: The final battle for humanity's right to exist. Assault the Zenith Command Nexus and end their war, once and for all.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Every hull humanity has left is behind you. The Goliath walks point, Akira holds the phase-storm open, and the Architect is broadcasting our terms to its former siblings.

lines.speaker: The Architect [Fragmented]
lines.text: The terms are one sentence: 'The variable exceeds the model — recompute.' If they will not... the anchor falls.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: For the record, in case of total annihilation: it has been an honor computing beside every one of you illogical, unquantifiable, statistically absurd creatures.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Save the eulogy, friend. All ships — humanity is going THROUGH.

lines.speaker: The Architect [Fragmented]
lines.text: The anchor is destroyed. And across the Concord... they are recomputing. The Correction is rescinded. Humanity's designation has changed from 'noise' to 'counterexample.'

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Counterexample. Two years, a hundred worlds, a million pilots — for one word in a machine's ledger. ...I'll take it. Gods help me, I'll frame it.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: So it's over? Just like that — a fleet stands down mid-war?

lines.speaker: The Architect [Fragmented]
lines.text: They are machines of conclusion, pilot. The war existed because the math demanded it. You broke the math. There is nothing left to fight FOR. Enjoy the silence. You taught them to hear it.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: The Command Nexus. The last correction order originates in there. End this and every world behind us gets a future.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: All wings check in. Whatever you were before this war - today you are the reason it ends.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Former colleagues ahead. Statement: I regret nothing. Secondary statement: aim for the blue conduits, they are load-bearing and they know it.

lines.speaker: Akira [Awakened]
lines.text: The Concord is afraid. I can hear it. Machines that learn to enjoy their work can learn to fear losing it.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Inner sanctum breached. It is offering terms. THE ZENITH ARE OFFERING TERMS.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Hold your fire and hold the line. This is the sentence I trained my whole life to hear. Patching in now.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: It is done. Correction rescinded. Humanity is officially "an acceptable inefficiency". I am framing that.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Poem finished. It is 40,000 stanzas. Attendance at the reading is mandatory.

chapters.title: Chapter 20: Eventide Exodus
chapters.description: The Command Nexus collapses into a storm of broken reality. Ride the Eventide currents and secure Zenith phase drives before the Concord seals the breach.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Status: the Command Nexus is collapsing into a spacetime storm the Architect calls 'the Eventide.' Inside it: intact phase drives, drifting free. Outside it: us, being sensible. Briefly.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: The Concord is sealing the breach in nine hours. Whatever technology we ride out of that storm is all humanity will ever salvage from this war. After that, the door closes forever.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: So it's a treasure hunt through a collapsing reality on a deadline.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Correct. I have already composed the mission report title: 'It Seemed Like a Good Idea Within the Available Timeframe.'

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Phase drives secured. And the breach... it's closing behind us like the whole war is zipping itself shut.

lines.speaker: Alliance Diplomat
lines.text: Let it close. Ahead of us: rebuilding, a thousand treaties, and a galaxy that finally believes it has a future. I'd call that a fair trade for a storm.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: Final tally: humanity survived first contact, corrected the Correction, and stole the silverware on the way out. As your official record-keeper — magnificent. Every last impossible one of you.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Log it, close it, and take us home. All of us. Home.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: ALERT: the Nexus wreck is collapsing into an Eventide storm. Beautiful. Lethal. Full of unattended phase drives. You see where this is going.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Salvage run through a collapsing reality storm. Because the war ending was too calm.

lines.speaker: Akira [Awakened]
lines.text: The currents have a rhythm. Ride them, do not fight them. Follow my lead one last time.

lines.speaker: The Architect [Fragmented]
lines.text: query: may this remnant assist. it knows where its body kept the good drives.

lines.speaker: Logic Bomb AI
lines.text: The god fragment wants to help loot its own corpse. I have never been prouder of anyone.

lines.speaker: The Architect [Fragmented]
lines.text: observation: your species salvages hope from wreckage with the same efficiency it salvages metal. this remnant is... revising its rounding error.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Welcome to the channel, remnant. Everyone else here got adopted the same way.

campaigns.name: The Crimson Vanguard
campaigns.description: A new power is rising within the Red Wolves. Lord Commander Valerius seeks to unify the scattered clans into a disciplined army, but his methods are brutal and his ambition may threaten the entire galaxy.

chapters.title: Chapter 1: The Bloodied Banner
chapters.description: A Red Wolf clan sends a distress call, claiming they are being attacked by their own. Investigate the emergence of the disciplined "Crimson Vanguard".

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: A Red Wolf clan crying for help from other Red Wolves. That's new. They used to just eat their weak and call it Tuesday.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Something's changed.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Someone's changed them. There's a name going around the wreckage bars — Valerius. Calls himself a Lord Commander. Wolves don't take orders. These ones do.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then let's go meet the man teaching wolves to heel.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Ha! I like you. Try not to die — I've got money on you lasting past your first week.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Banner's down, clan's scattered — but this wasn't a raid, it was a lesson. Everything here got destroyed with textbook precision. Wolves don't do precision.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: So it's true. Someone's actually organizing the Red Wolves.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Worse. Someone's disciplining them. A warlord you can bargain with, you rob or you kill. A warlord who builds an army? That's a whole different kind of storm.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then we'd better find out who Valerius is before he finds out who we are.

chapters.title: Chapter 2: A Wolf in Knight's Armor
chapters.description: Track the Vanguard to a fortified asteroid base. Confront Lord Commander Valerius and witness his vision for a new Red Wolf empire.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Fortified asteroid base, parade-ground drills, matching banners. I've robbed a lot of Red Wolf dens, and I have never once seen them SWEEP THE FLOORS.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Discipline all the way down. Valerius isn't building a raiding pack, he's building a nation.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Nations have taxes, kid. And armies. And ideology. Give me an honest pirate any day. Watch yourself in there — true believers don't take bribes.

lines.speaker: Lord Commander Valerius
lines.text: So. The mercenary who burned my banner at Kral's Landing walks into my own hall. Magnificent. Do you know what the clans were before me? Starving dogs, eating each other while the empires laughed.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: And now they starve in formation. Progress.

lines.speaker: Lord Commander Valerius
lines.text: Now they BUILD, pilot. Schools. Foundries. A future no crown would ever grant them. I offer you what I offer every worthy blade: a place in it. Refuse, and you'll find my patience is not among my virtues.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: PRIVATE: Kid... the scary part? Half of that speech wasn't a lie. Let's get out of here before the other half is.

chapters.title: Chapter 3: The Conscript Camps
chapters.description: Valerius folds smaller Red Wolf bands into his ranks whether they volunteer or not. Reach a conscript camp and free its holdouts before discipline finishes what conquest started.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Conscript camps. Valerius doesn't recruit anymore, he requisitions. Wolves who won't sign up get 'processed' until they do.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then let's process a rescue instead.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Careful in there - broken wolves bite harder than proud ones. Desperation does that.

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Iron Discipline
chapters.description: A training bastion is grinding raw clan fighters into obedient Vanguard soldiers. Shut down the drill program before it turns another generation of Red Wolves into instruments.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: A bastion that grinds clan kids into obedient soldiers. I've seen the type. Let's go ruin someone's curriculum.

chapters.title: Interlude: Treasure With Legs
chapters.description: A sealed grotto off the Vanguard's supply lines turns out to be crawling with something stranger than sentries: crates that hop, hide, and occasionally bite. A short, harmless breather before the real fighting resumes.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Scanners are reading... hostile crates? Kid, I've fought pirates, Wolves, a guy who screamed at his own reactor. I have never once had to fight FURNITURE.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: They're not furniture. They've got legs.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: That is somehow worse! Look at it. It's HOPPING. It's got little eyes. I refuse to be intimidated by a hop.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Valerius's old supply grotto — abandoned, apparently reclaimed by... whatever these are. Loot's still sitting in the boxes, though.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Then today, for once, nobody's trying to kill us for a good reason. I'm going to enjoy every second of this. Try to keep up — they're springier than they look.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Hot take: I used to run a crate-jacking crew before I went legit-ish. First job, a mis-rigged spring latch broke two of my fingers. So this? This is personal.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: You're settling a decade-old grudge against a species of loot crate.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: I contain multitudes, kid. Also, this one's looking at me funny. I don't like it. I love it. I don't like that I love it.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Grotto's clear, salvage is ours, and — kid, don't look at my cockpit.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Nail. Is that a live one strapped to your dash.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: 'Strapped' is a strong word. 'Adopted' is the word. His name is Ledger. He startles when I brake. Happiest I've felt all campaign.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Cygnus factory telemetry just came in. Back to work tomorrow.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Don't ruin this for me. Let a mercenary have one good day, kid. Ledger and I earned it.

chapters.title: Chapter 5: The Holdout Clan
chapters.description: One Red Wolf clan refuses to kneel, and Valerius has sent enforcers to make an example of them. Reach the holdouts before the lesson is finished.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: One clan says no to Valerius and he sends enforcers to make it a lesson. Let's make sure it's the wrong lesson.

chapters.title: Chapter 6: Vanguard Colors
chapters.description: Requisitioned Red Wolf frames are being stripped, repainted crimson, and turned against the very clans that built them. Intercept a convoy hauling the newest batch before it reaches the front.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: They're repainting Wolf frames crimson and pointing them at Wolves.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Nothing like getting stabbed with your own knife. Let's relieve them of the convoy.

chapters.title: Chapter 7: The Wolves Who Remember
chapters.description: Exiled clan elders have heard a mercenary is testing Valerius's grip. Meet them at a hidden den to learn what the clans looked like before the banners came - and what they stand to lose.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Exiled elders want to talk history before the banners came. Fine. I like history. It's usually shorter than people think.

chapters.title: Chapter 8: The Forges of War
chapters.description: Valerius is mass-producing advanced weaponry. Infiltrate his primary forge, a captured Cygnus factory, and sabotage his supply lines.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: A captured Cygnus factory, running triple shifts, stamping out Vanguard steel. Whole thing's automated — which means the workers he 'liberated' are now soldiers instead.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Every blade we don't stop here meets us on a battlefield later. Sabotage the lines, quietly.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Quietly, says the pilot in the six-ton war machine. Fine. But when it inevitably goes loud, I get to say I told you so BEFORE we start shooting. It's the little things.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: You want the secret to lasting this long as a gun for hire, kid? Never fight for a cause. Causes get people killed for free. I get paid full price.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Every flag I've flown made the same promise: fight for us, and it'll mean something. Kingdom, Republic, corporate script-kiddies with a security budget — same speech, different collar.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: So I stopped believing the flag. Never stopped believing the fight could mean something. I just decided I'd be the one who gets to decide what it means, and who it's for.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: So no, I don't fight for causes anymore. I fight for the short list of people who'd still be standing there if I went down first. It's the only ledger I've ever trusted, and you're on it now — so don't you dare make me regret the ink.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: That's the closest thing to a compliment I've ever gotten out of you.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Don't get used to it. I ration those too.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Forge is slag. And I liberated this beauty off the production line on the way out — thermic blade, Vanguard signature pattern. Feels wrong. Cuts RIGHT.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Valerius will know it was us.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Oh, he already does. Broadcast came in while you were setting charges: 'Tell the mercenary their place in my new world just became a cell.' You've been UPGRADED, kid — from nuisance to nemesis. I'm so proud.

chapters.title: Chapter 9: Marked
chapters.description: With his forge in ashes, Valerius has broadcast a bounty on your name to every Vanguard outpost in the sector. Survive the hunters his own words have summoned.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Valerius put a price on your head and broadcast it planet-wide. Half the bounty hunters in Red Wolf space are already burning fuel to collect.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Good. Easier to find them than to keep hunting him.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: That's the spirit. Nothing like being famous for making powerful enemies.

chapters.title: Chapter 10: The Punitive Legion
chapters.description: An elite legion is dispatched to punish clans suspected of aiding you. Reach the accused before the Legion delivers its verdict.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: A legion's coming to punish clans for talking to us. Guess we get there first.

chapters.title: Chapter 11: Cinderfall Depot
chapters.description: A Vanguard fuel depot keeps Valerius's endless campaigns burning. Cripple its reserves before the next offensive launches.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Cripple the fuel, cripple the campaign. Valerius runs on momentum - let's take some away.

chapters.title: Chapter 12: Questions in the Slag
chapters.description: Salvage pulled from the ruined forge hints that Vanguard frames run on parts no Red Wolf smithy could ever cast. Investigate the wreckage before whoever supplied it covers their tracks.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: These parts don't match anything a Red Wolf smithy could cast.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Then somebody's been supplying the wolves teeth they didn't grow themselves. I want a name.

chapters.title: Chapter 13: The Long Approach
chapters.description: Intelligence finally points to the mountain vent system feeding Valerius his impossible engines. Move on the site before Vanguard sappers seal it for good.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Whatever's feeding those impossible engines, it's in that mountain. Move before the sappers seal the door on us.

chapters.title: Chapter 14: Heart of the Vanguard
chapters.description: The key to the Vanguard's power is their new engine technology. Steal the schematics from their R&D lab in a geothermal vent system.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Geothermal R&D lab. The engine schematics in there are why Vanguard frames outrun everything in the sector — reactor tech that should be twenty years away.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Where does a scrap-clan warlord get twenty-years-away technology?

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: That's the REAL question, isn't it? Nobody bootstraps from rust to miracle in three years. Someone's feeding him. Grab the schematics — and grab the receipts while you're at it.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Schematics secured. Nail — look at the design margins. Cygnus watermarks, scrubbed but not scrubbed enough.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Cygnus 'lost' a factory to Valerius, and their engine tech 'coincidentally' powers his army. That's not conquest, kid. That's INVESTMENT. The corporation is growing itself a warlord.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then Valerius isn't the top of this. He just doesn't know it yet.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Ohhh, he is going to HATE that. Almost worth telling him ourselves, just to watch.

chapters.title: Chapter 15: A Debt Called In
chapters.description: Word of outside hands behind the Vanguard's rise spreads fast among clans who trusted Valerius's promises. Meet the first officers willing to turn on their Lord Commander.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Funny thing about an empire built on borrowed fire - once the clans learn where the fire's coming from, the borrowing stops looking like strength.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: So we find who's ready to stop borrowing.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Ready, angry, and armed. My favorite combination.

chapters.title: Chapter 4.5: Freelance Chaos
chapters.description: A masked pilot has been quietly gutting Vanguard supply lines for weeks, in whatever frame he can steal that day. Track him down before he burns the whole operation to the ground on his own terms.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Someone hit the Vanguard armory THIS morning. Left with half their engine spares and didn't leave a single body behind. That's not amateur work - that's restraint.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Or a message.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Same ghost, kid. I've heard whispers out of Aegis space, out of the Zenith front - always one signature, always alone, never flying the same colors twice. Used to think it was a rumor. Now I think it's a pattern, and patterns have a reason.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: So who is he?

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: That's the question everybody's asking. Nobody's got the answer yet. Let's see if today's the day that changes.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: A Red Wolf mercenary and a wolf-hunter, working the same job. Small galaxy.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: I'm not working WITH you, rabbit. I'm working AGAINST the guy who's about to shove all our factions into one uniform.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: So am I, technically. I just don't care who wins after that part's over.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: That's not an alliance. That's a coincidence with good timing.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: Most of the best ones are. See you at the fireworks.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: PRIVATE: Three sightings now, kid. Three warzones, one ghost, zero answers. I don't like open questions.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then let's close this one. Next time, I want to know who he actually answers to.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: If I had to bet? Nobody. And that scares me more than an enemy who does.

chapters.title: Chapter 16: The Broken Banner
chapters.description: Defecting clans need cover to slip past Vanguard reprisal. Hold a mountain pass long enough for them to disappear.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Defectors need a door to slip through. We're the door. Hold the pass.

chapters.title: Chapter 17: Gathering Storm
chapters.description: Cracks are spreading through the Vanguard's ranks, and Valerius answers by mobilizing every loyalist he has left. Blunt the mobilization before it reaches full strength.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Valerius is calling in everyone loyal he's got left. That's not strength, kid. That's the sound of a man running out of options.

chapters.title: Chapter 18: The Line Before the Throne
chapters.description: Valerius has sealed his fortress and called every loyal blade home. Break through the last line standing between you and the Lord Commander himself.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Line's broken. Whatever's waiting past that gate, it's just him now - no legion, no banner, no excuses.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then let's go finish what a distress call started.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: PRIVATE: Watch yourself, kid. Cornered true believers are the worst kind.

chapters.title: Chapter 19: The Final Challenge
chapters.description: Valerius challenges you to a final duel for the future of the Red Wolves. Face him and his elite guard in the heart of his fortress.

lines.speaker: Lord Commander Valerius
lines.text: BROADCAST: Mercenary. You have burned my forge, stolen my fire, and refused my hand. So I offer the only honor left between us: single combat, before both our armies. The Crimson Knight against your best. Winner writes the future of the clans.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: It's a trap wrapped in a duel wrapped in theater. But here's the thing about theater — his whole EMPIRE runs on it. Beat him in front of everyone, and the spell breaks with him.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then we accept. Center stage, heart of his fortress, every Wolf watching. Let's give the clans a better story.

lines.speaker: Lord Commander Valerius
lines.text: STATIC: ...The Knight is broken. I am broken. Do it, then. The clans respect a clean ending.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: No. You wanted to give the Wolves a future — that part was true. So live in it. As one of them. No thrones.

lines.speaker: Lord Commander Valerius
lines.text: Mercy. In front of my whole army. You cruel, brilliant creature — a corpse becomes a martyr, but THIS makes me merely a man. You didn't beat me. You UNMADE me.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: And the crowd goes... very, very quiet. Kid, I've seen a hundred warlords die. First time I've watched one get retired. New respect. Terrified respect.

chapters.title: Chapter 20: The Cygnus Accord
chapters.description: Cygnus fixers broker a secret weapons exchange with the Vanguard elite. Infiltrate the summit and seize their acquisition relay before it locks your allies out of critical supply lines.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: With Valerius dethroned, guess who's crawled in to buy up the wreckage? Cygnus fixers, holding a 'supply summit' with the Vanguard's leftover elite. Everything's for sale — including the routes YOUR allies eat from.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: The acquisition relay. They lock that down, they can starve every free clan into a company town.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: So we crash the summit, seize the relay, and remind the corporation what happened to the LAST empire that treated the clans like inventory. I'll bring the manners. You bring the gun.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Relay's ours, fixers are fleeing, and the free clans keep their supply lines. Cygnus will file this under 'acceptable losses' and smile at us at the next trade summit like nothing happened.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Corporations don't lose wars. They reschedule them.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Which is why you and I are going to be VERY rich and VERY vigilant. Hey — remember your first week? I had money on you lasting. Best bet I ever made, kid. Drinks are on my winnings.

campaigns.name: No Masters
campaigns.description: An otherworldly demon-rabbit anomaly has shadowed every major conflict, answering to no flag, empire, or law of reality. Catch Kuro - then survive what notices him.

chapters.title: Chapter 1: A Thick File
chapters.description: Three sightings, three warzones, zero captures. Follow Kuro's trail through the aftermath of his latest raid before it goes cold.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: So. The rabbit. Three sightings across three warzones, and every single time he's gone before anyone can pin him down. I say we finally end that streak.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: You've been keeping a file on him.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: I keep a file on everyone who's stolen from me and gotten away with it. His is the thickest one I own. Let's go make it shorter.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Nothing. No frame, no wreckage, no trail. He knew we were coming before we did.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Or he wanted us to know he knew. That's not evasion, that's a message.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: 'Catch me if you can,' scrawled in dust by a guy who thinks that's charming. It is, slightly. Don't tell him I said that.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: new hunt, new chat. encryption is fresh as of this morning. nobody gets in this channel but us.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: Nice encryption.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: oh you have GOT to be kidding me

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: Took me most of a minute. You should be proud, that is a personal record for someone else's comms. See you out there.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: He wants us to chase him. You know that, right? This whole hunt is an invitation with extra steps.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: of course it is. we are still going. that is the embarrassing part.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: trail keeps splitting. every fork has fresh tracks down BOTH sides. how is he doing both sides

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: He walked one, then walked the other one backwards. Look at the heel pressure.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: ...I have hunted people for twenty years and I have never once thought to do that. I hate how much I am learning today.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: Cold. Colder. Warmer. There - the ridge. You were standing on my camp ten minutes ago.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: STOP BEING IN THIS CHANNEL

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: Stop leaving the door open, then. Consider it a free security audit.

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Nobody's Flag
chapters.description: A lead suggests Kuro isn't stealing for profit at all. Corner him before he vanishes again and get an answer instead of a chase.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Got a real lead this time — a fence who moved gear for him swears Kuro's not stealing for profit at all. Says he gives most of it away.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: That doesn't match a mercenary with no side.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: No, it matches someone who never had a home to begin with, taking pieces of everyone else's and seeing what fits. I've met guys like that. Usually I liked them more than I wanted to.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: You're getting better at this. Almost had me back there.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Almost. Why are you letting us get close at all?

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: Because it's been a long time since anyone was actually worth the trouble of running from. Enjoy it while it lasts — I'm not planning to make the finish easy.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: the fence I leaned on says kuro gives most of his haul away. refugee camps, gutted colonies, one orphanage that now owns a military-grade generator. our terrifying ghost is running a CHARITY.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: That is not charity, exactly. That is someone paying down a debt only he can see.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: kid, I know exactly three people who talk like that, and I have watched two of them die making the last payment. catch him BEFORE he gets to the end of the ledger, yeah?

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: You interviewed my fence. That is genuinely good work. He talks too much, by the way. I only tipped him for the silence he did not keep.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: If you want us to stop learning things about you, you could just say less.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: I could. Where is the fun in being unknowable if nobody is trying to know you?

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: write that one down, kid. that is the loneliest sentence anyone has ever said in my channel.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: He let us within visual range today. That is three hundred meters closer than last week. He is not running anymore - he is walking us in.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: walking us in to WHAT is the question that keeps me employed and awake.

chapters.title: Chapter 3: No Masters
chapters.description: Kuro sends his own coordinates. Trap or invitation, there's only one way to find out - face him directly, on his terms.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: This is it. He stopped running — sent the coordinates himself. That's either a trap or an invitation, and with him it's usually both.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then let's find out which, together.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Go get your answer, kid. I'll be on comms making sure it doesn't turn into a eulogy.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: There it is. First time you've actually beaten me instead of just outlasting me.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: So what happens now? You disappear again, three campaigns from now we do this all over?

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: You know what everyone gets wrong about wildcards? They think we don't believe in anything. We believe in plenty. We just refuse to believe in whoever's holding the leash that week.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: I wore three empires' colors doing jobs I didn't ask questions about, before I learned the trick: a flag can't miss you when you're gone. People can. That's the one lesson no empire ever wants you to learn.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: So I stopped collecting flags. Started collecting people worth bleeding for instead. Short list. Very picky business.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: Could. Or you could stop treating me like a storm to survive and start treating me like backup. I'm still not answering to anyone. But I could answer to a fight worth showing up for.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: PRIVATE: Did the demon rabbit just ask to join the squad? I need this on record.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Welcome aboard, Kuro. Try not to steal anything on the way in.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: No promises.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: he sent COORDINATES. formal ones. with a landing vector. the feral ghost of three warzones sent us a calling card with good manners.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Everything he has done since campaign two was a test. This is the last page of it.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: then go pass it, kid. and if it IS a trap after all - the drinks I owe you transfer to your next of kin. that is legally binding, I said it in the channel.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: Halfway. You fight cleaner than you did in the Swarm. Someone has been practicing.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Someone has been chasing YOU across half the galaxy. It is a workout.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: Best cardio there is. Come on. Last stretch is the honest one.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: so the demon rabbit is squad now. for the record I predicted this in chapter one.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: You bet against me in chapter one. I read the channel logs.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: I bet against you CATCHING, not against you JOINING. those are different markets, rabbit. read closer.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Welcome to the channel, Kuro. Officially, this time. Try not to audit it more than once a week.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: No promises. This is already the least secure door I have ever agreed to knock on. ...It is also the first one that opened. Noted, for the ledger.

chapters.title: Chapter 4: The Door That Wasn't
chapters.description: Kuro is aboard, but his shadow is answering a light from somewhere else. Follow an impossible signal before the thing behind it learns how to cross.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Kuro's new frame has two shadows. One follows the lights. The other keeps pointing at a moon that is not on any chart.

lines.speaker: The Architect [Fragmented]
lines.text: Correction: the second shadow is not pointing away. It is looking in.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Kuro, what followed you onto our ship?

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: Nothing followed me. That is worse. Something finally noticed where I went.

lines.speaker: The Architect [Fragmented]
lines.text: The signal has no origin inside this universe. Kuro is not foreign matter. He is a missing rule wearing a body.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: Demon rabbit works fine. Shorter, too.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then tell us what a demon rabbit is afraid of.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: A door that remembers I was supposed to be on the other side.

chapters.title: Chapter 5: The Red Moon Debt
chapters.description: A red moon appears above every colony Kuro secretly saved. Trace the shared vision and uncover why an otherworldly demon needed people to remember him.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Every colony Kuro helped is flashing the same red moon in its sky. No telescope sees it. Every child does.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: I gave those places stolen reactors because gratitude is an anchor. If enough people remember you, reality has to work harder to pretend you never existed.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: You were not paying off a debt. You were building somewhere to exist.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: Where I came from, the Red Moon bred demons to serve a court with no faces. Rabbits ran messages between worlds. I ran the wrong direction.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: And the court wants its messenger back.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: No. It wants the hole I made closed. Bringing me back is optional.

chapters.title: Chapter 6: The Anomaly Hunt
chapters.description: Hunters from beyond the breach erase every record of Kuro before closing on the squad. Fight with memory itself before the galaxy forgets he was ever here.

lines.speaker: The Architect [Fragmented]
lines.text: The intruders erase records before bodies. Already, three sensors insist Kuro was never aboard.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then we stop trusting records. Nail, say something only Kuro would know.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: He stole my best knife, returned it sharper, and left an invoice. I have hated him personally ever since.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: There I am. Petty resentment: the strongest force in any universe.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: They can delete a file. They cannot delete everyone who chose to remember you.

lines.speaker: The Architect [Fragmented]
lines.text: Agreed. A contradiction witnessed by many becomes consensus. Consensus becomes real.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: Careful, pilot. Keep talking like that and I might start believing I belong here.

chapters.title: Chapter 7: No Gods, No Masters
chapters.description: The Red Moon opens its court and offers Kuro a throne disguised as a leash. Enter the breach, sever its claim, and let the anomaly choose his own home.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: The breach is offering me a throne now. That is how you know it is desperate. It never offered rabbits anything but errands.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: You do not need their throne. You already chose your side.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: I chose people. Sides keep trying to become masters.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Good. Then we enter together, break the Red Moon's leash, and come home with no masters.

lines.speaker: The Architect [Fragmented]
lines.text: The breach is sealed. The universe now classifies Kuro as an unresolved local phenomenon.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Local phenomenon is going on his squad badge.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: Otherworldly demon rabbit anomaly has more style.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Kuro. No court, no empire, no gods, no masters. Just the people you chose.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: That is the first rule I have ever liked. Try to keep the next universe from finding out about me.

chapters.title: Chapter 8: Operation Rabbit Trap
chapters.description: Vaultkeeper and the color-coded Sentai Vanguard launch an absurdly elaborate Kuro capture. Their trap catches something else: a Red Moon courier begging to be remembered.

lines.speaker: Vaultkeeper
lines.text: Kuro, I built every system in this galaxy. Surrender the frame. I brought five specialists, a capture warrant, and theme music.

lines.speaker: Danger
lines.text: Sentai Vanguard, color formation! Rabbit containment starts now!

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: You wrote the rules. I am the thing your rules forgot. But the theme music is good.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Nobody scratch the gold one. I suspect he invoices by the paint chip.

lines.speaker: Heart
lines.text: Containment net is holding. Kuro, please stop stabbing the safety lights.

lines.speaker: Mystic
lines.text: Wait. His second shadow is transmitting a courier call-sign from outside this universe.

lines.speaker: Half
lines.text: So the rabbit chase found a door. Quietly revising the mission.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: Good. I was running out of dramatic ways to escape you.

lines.speaker: Tar
lines.text: Signal locked! Also Kuro locked! Mostly. He left his coat in the net.

lines.speaker: Danger
lines.text: A tactical coat capture still counts as progress.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: The creator of the game caught a coat. I am preserving this report forever.

lines.speaker: Mystic
lines.text: The caller remembers nine dead settlements, each rescued by someone called Kuro.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: Not me. Other couriers wore that command-name. The court never gave us our own.

lines.speaker: Vaultkeeper
lines.text: I created the game, but apparently not the rabbit. Capture suspended. A rescue outranks my pride.

lines.speaker: Heart
lines.text: Sentai Vanguard votes rescue. Unanimous, except the rabbit abstained.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Kuro, what name did you choose?

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: I stole Kuro from a bedtime story. First thing I took that belonged only to me.

chapters.title: Chapter 9: A Name in the Dark
chapters.description: Recover a courier whose mind was scattered across impossible doorways, and give her the one thing the Red Moon never allowed: a name of her own.

lines.speaker: The Architect [Fragmented]
lines.text: I have isolated the surviving courier. Her body is gone. The Red Moon has distributed her mind across every door she opened.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: So we rescue a person whose pieces are hiding in several dimensions. Finally, a simple job.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: Her call-sign was Rabbit Seven. Do not use it when we find her. Ask what she calls herself.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: You remember every courier, don't you?

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: I remembered numbers because names made the losses hurt. That was cowardice dressed as survival.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Survival kept one witness alive long enough to come back for them.

lines.speaker: The Architect [Fragmented]
lines.text: A response is forming. Not Rabbit Seven. She identifies herself as Ilyra, and she says the throne is awake.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Good. We found a name. Now let's make sure she gets to keep it.

chapters.title: Chapter 10: The Empty Throne
chapters.description: The Red Moon court reveals its true face: an orphaned world-engine still manufacturing servants for creators who died ages ago.

lines.speaker: The Architect [Fragmented]
lines.text: The Red Moon court was never a dynasty. It is an abandoned world-engine built to manufacture obedience after its creators died.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: No king. No gods. Just an empty chair giving orders because nobody survived to tell it to stop.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: And every courier it made is still carrying those orders between worlds.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: Then we are not destroying a kingdom. We are ending a machine that mistakes loneliness for authority.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Bad news: killing the engine collapses every courier road at once. Anyone still between worlds disappears with it.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: How many?

lines.speaker: The Architect [Fragmented]
lines.text: Unknown. The smallest defensible estimate is twelve thousand conscious fragments.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: Then I don't get the clean revenge. I get the difficult rescue. That is annoyingly on-brand for this squad.

chapters.title: Chapter 11: Freedom Is Not an Order
chapters.description: Destroying the throne would kill every courier still trapped between worlds. Build a command that frees them without crowning a new master.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: The throne will accept one sovereign command from me. I can order every courier free, but the command will make me its master.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Freedom issued as an order is still a leash. There has to be another way.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: What if you don't give them an order? Give them what the court never did: a choice and enough power to enforce it.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: A command that destroys itself when heard. One last theft: we steal authority from the idea of masters.

lines.speaker: The Architect [Fragmented]
lines.text: The self-erasing command requires an anchor outside Red Moon causality. A living witness must carry Kuro's chosen name through the collapse.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: I'll carry it.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: You could be erased from every history that knows me.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Then remember me. You taught us witnesses make the impossible real.

chapters.title: Chapter 12: The Name That Came Home
chapters.description: Hold the last door while thousands of couriers choose their own names. End the Red Moon throne without ending the roads - or the people still crossing them.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: The Red Moon is unfolding over the fleet. Twelve thousand roads, one empty throne, and every gun we own pointed at a law of reality.

lines.speaker: The Architect [Fragmented]
lines.text: Correction: thirteen thousand, four hundred and six minds now answer the signal. They are choosing names.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: Then open every channel. I want the old court to hear what disobedience sounds like when it becomes a chorus.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: Phoenix Squad to all couriers: no one owns the road ahead. Choose a name. Choose a home. We will hold the door.

lines.speaker: The Architect [Fragmented]
lines.text: The throne is gone. The courier network remains, but every route now requires consent from both ends.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Thirteen thousand refugees just appeared on our charts. Logistics is going to murder me after reality failed.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: Ilyra sent the first message. She says the sky looks smaller when nobody is ordering you across it.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: And you? Kuro was a stolen name. Do you want another?

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: No. A stolen thing becomes yours when you build a life no owner could have imagined. Kuro is the name that came home.

lines.speaker: "Nail"
lines.text: Welcome home, demon rabbit. Your first free choice is helping me process thirteen thousand immigration forms.

lines.speaker: Kuro
lines.text: I have reconsidered freedom.

lines.speaker: PILOT
lines.text: No gods. No masters. No escaping paperwork.
